docs.title: Translating NodeMT5 docs
docs.text: The docs are internationalised with mkdocs-static-i18n (suffix structure). English is the source; 27 target languages are configured. This page is the skeleton for translators.

docs.title: How it works (the mechanism)
docs.text:
• Language switcher — the globe menu in the header lists every configured language; it's generated automatically from the plugin config in mkdocs.yml.
  • Fallback — a page with no translation falls back to English, so every language already works end-to-end. You translate pages one at a time; nothing breaks in the meantime.
  • URLs — English is at the root (/NodeMT5/…), each language under its locale (/NodeMT5/zh/…, /NodeMT5/ja/…, …).

You don't pre-create blank files for every page — that would hide the English fallback behind empty pages. Create a translation file only when you actually translate that page.

docs.title: How to translate a page
docs.text:
Suffix structure: put the translation next to the English file, with the locale before .md.

docs/All_Guides/GETTING_STARTED.md        # English (source)
docs/All_Guides/GETTING_STARTED.zh.md     # 简体中文
docs/All_Guides/GETTING_STARTED.ja.md     # 日本語
docs/index.md                             # English home
docs/index.ja.md                          # 日本語 home

Steps:

  1. Copy the English page.md to page.<locale>.md.
  2. Translate the prose. Keep unchanged: code blocks, API names, enum constants, file paths, links, and front-matter keys (hide:, description:).
  3. Build (python -m mkdocs build) or serve (python -m mkdocs serve) and check the page under /<locale>/.

Translate in this order (highest value first): index → All_Guides/GETTING_STARTED → MT5_For_Beginners → Your_First_Project → GLOSSARY → RETURN_CODES_REFERENCE, then the rest. The deep API/method pages are read mostly in English and can come last.

docs.title: Right-to-left languages
docs.text: ar, fa, ur, he are configured with direction: rtl — the theme flips layout automatically for those locales. Keep code/paths LTR (Markdown handles this).

docs.title: The Concurrency Model — How NodeMT5 Executes
docs.text: NodeMT5 is built on Promises and async/await. Unary calls are async functions you await; streams hand you a callback plus a Subscription you cancel. Everything runs on Node's single-threaded event loop — no threads, no locks.

docs.title: 🎯 Two shapes of call
docs.text: Shape What it is How you consume it Unary (request / response) getAccountSummary(), getSymbolTick(), placeOrder() await it; the promise resolves with the result (or rejects) Server stream onSymbolTick(), streamTicks() pass a callback; it fires per payload; keep the returned Subscription and call unsubscribe()

docs.title: Unary — await
docs.text:
Every unary method returns a Promise. There is nothing to poll; the gRPC round-trip happens inside the await.

const a = await service.getAccountSummary();     // resolves with AccountInfo
console.log(a.balance, a.equity);

const quote = await service.getSymbolTick('EURUSD');

A failure rejects the promise with an MrpcError — catch it:

try {
  const t = await sugar.buyMarket('EURUSD', 0.10);
} catch (e) {
  console.error('rejected:', e.message);
}

docs.title: Streaming — callback + Subscription
docs.text:
A stream does not return data; it calls your callback on each payload and returns a handle to stop it.

const sub = service.streamTicks(['EURUSD'], (q) => {
  console.log(q.bid, q.ask);
}, (err) => console.error(err.message));

setTimeout(() => sub.unsubscribe(), 30_000);   // stop after 30s

docs.title: 🧵 One event loop, no threads
docs.text:
Node runs your JavaScript on one thread. await doesn't spawn a thread — it yields the event loop until the I/O completes, then resumes. That means:

  • No data races on your own variables within a synchronous run — but another callback or timer can run between your awaits. Don't assume state is unchanged across an await.
  • A long synchronous loop blocks everything (including stream callbacks). Keep callbacks short; offload heavy CPU work.
  • Stream callbacks are invoked as payloads arrive, interleaved with your unary awaits on the same loop.

docs.title: 🔀 Running calls concurrently
docs.text:
await in sequence is serial. To run independent calls at once, start them together and Promise.all:

// serial — two round-trips back to back
const bid = await sugar.getBid('EURUSD');
const ask = await sugar.getAsk('EURUSD');

// concurrent — both in flight together
const [b, a] = await Promise.all([
  sugar.getBid('EURUSD'),
  sugar.getAsk('EURUSD'),
]);

The SDK itself does this internally — e.g. getPriceInfo fetches the tick and the symbol params with Promise.all.

docs.title: ⏱️ Timeouts
docs.text:
Every unary call carries an internal gRPC deadline; on expiry the promise rejects.

  • Default deadline — 30_000 ms. Set on MT5Account.callTimeoutMs; tune it for a slow link:
sugar.account().callTimeoutMs = 60_000;   // 60s for every unary call
  • Per-call override. Methods that can run long accept a timeoutMs argument (e.g. symbolParamsMany(symbol?, timeoutMs) defaults to 120_000; the low-level symbolInfo* take an optional timeoutMs).
  • Connect takes timeoutSeconds in its options (default 60); reconnect uses 70_000 ms.
  • MT5Sugar manages timeouts for you — its methods take no timeout argument.

docs.title: 🧹 Lifecycle
docs.text:
const sugar = MT5Sugar.create('mt5.mrpc.pro', 443, apiKey);
await sugar.quickConnect(login, password, server);   // obtains the terminal session
// … use it …
await sugar.service().disconnect(true);              // stop the terminal + free resources

Always unsubscribe streams and disconnect when done — an open stream or warm terminal keeps resources alive on the gateway.

docs.title: Enums Usage Reference — Node
docs.text: The generated protobuf enums are plain JavaScript namespace objects: Namespace.CONSTANT → number. This page shows which namespace holds which enum, and how to use them at each layer.

docs.title: 🧭 How protobuf enums look in Node
docs.text:
import { TradingHelperPb } from '@metarpc/nodemt5';

TradingHelperPb.TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE.TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY   // === 0 (a number)

Each *Pb module is re-exported from the package. An enum is an object mapping names to numbers; you pass the value into a setter or compare it against a getter.

docs.title: 📇 The enums you'll use most
docs.text:
Enum Namespace Example value Order type TradingHelperPb.TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY (0) Account double property AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoDoublePropertyType ACCOUNT_BALANCE Account integer property AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType ACCOUNT_LEVERAGE Account string property AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoStringPropertyType ACCOUNT_SERVER Symbol double property MarketInfoPb.SymbolInfoDoubleProperty SYMBOL_POINT, SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_VALUE Symbol integer property MarketInfoPb.SymbolInfoIntegerProperty SYMBOL_DIGITS, SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL Symbol string property MarketInfoPb.SymbolInfoStringProperty SYMBOL_DESCRIPTION, SYMBOL_CURRENCY_BASE Account trade mode AccountHelperPb.MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode MRPC_ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO Position type MarketInfoPb.BMT5_ENUM_POSITION_TYPE BMT5_POSITION_TYPE_BUY (0) Order state MarketInfoPb.BMT5_ENUM_ORDER_STATE — Day of week MarketInfoPb.BMT5_ENUM_DAY_OF_WEEK —

Namespaces follow the proto service the message belongs to. When unsure, open the stub (package/*_pb.js) or use the Protobuf Inspector.

docs.title: 🔽 Low level (MT5Account) — pass the enum directly
docs.text:
import { MT5Account, AccountInformationPb, MarketInfoPb } from '@metarpc/nodemt5';

const bal = await account.accountInfoDouble(
  AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoDoublePropertyType.ACCOUNT_BALANCE,
);

const req = new MarketInfoPb.SymbolInfoIntegerRequest();
req.setSymbol('EURUSD');
req.setType(MarketInfoPb.SymbolInfoIntegerProperty.SYMBOL_DIGITS);
const digits = (await account.symbolInfoInteger(req)).getRequestedValue();

docs.title: 🟦 Mid level (MT5Service) — same enum, plain call
docs.text:
const digits = await service.getSymbolInteger('EURUSD', MarketInfoPb.SymbolInfoIntegerProperty.SYMBOL_DIGITS);
const point  = await service.getSymbolDouble('EURUSD', MarketInfoPb.SymbolInfoDoubleProperty.SYMBOL_POINT);
const server = await service.getAccountString(AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoStringPropertyType.ACCOUNT_SERVER);

docs.title: 🟩 High level (MT5Sugar) — enums hidden
docs.text:
The sugar layer wraps the common properties so you rarely touch an enum:

const digits  = await sugar.getSymbolDigits('EURUSD');       // SYMBOL_DIGITS inside
const minStop = await sugar.getMinStopLevel('EURUSD');       // SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL inside

docs.title: 🛒 Order-type enum (trading)
docs.text:
TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY = 0   SELL = 1   BUY_LIMIT = 2   SELL_LIMIT = 3
BUY_STOP = 4   SELL_STOP = 5   BUY_STOP_LIMIT = 6   SELL_STOP_LIMIT = 7   CLOSE_BY = 8

The friendly layers accept the string action instead — 'BUY', 'SELL_LIMIT', … — and map it to this enum for you (MT5Service.placeOrder, MT5Sugar.buyMarket).

docs.title: 👤 Position-type enum
docs.text:
BMT5_POSITION_TYPE_BUY = 0   BMT5_POSITION_TYPE_SELL = 1

Position.type is this raw value: p.type === 0 is a long.

docs.title: ⚠️ Gotchas
docs.text:
• Values are numbers, not strings — compare getter() === Namespace.CONST, don't compare names.
  • The Pb modules are typed any — TypeScript won't catch a wrong enum/namespace name; it fails at runtime. Verify names against the stubs (see Protobuf Inspector).
  • Namespace names can surprise you — e.g. symbol properties are SymbolInfoDoubleProperty (not SymbolInfoDouble), and the trade-mode enum is MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode with MRPC_-prefixed values.

docs.title: 📒 Complete enum catalog
docs.text: Every enum in the generated stubs (71 total), grouped by the *Pb namespace it lives on. Access a value as Namespace.ENUM.CONSTANT (e.g. AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoDoublePropertyType.ACCOUNT_BALANCE). A few giant enums (error codes, symbol industries) are linked rather than dumped. Regenerate this list anytime with node examples/demos/helpers/17_protobuf_inspector.js enum <Name>.

docs.title: Getting Started with NodeMT5
docs.text: Quick setup — connect to MetaTrader 5 from Node.js in a few minutes.

docs.title: What is NodeMT5?
docs.text:
NodeMT5 is a Node.js / TypeScript client for MetaTrader 5 accounts over the MetaRPC gRPC API (mt5.mrpc.pro:443). It's organised in three layers you can mix freely:

  • MT5Account — raw gRPC, protobuf in/out, full control.
  • MT5Service — typed objects, plain arguments.
  • MT5Sugar — one-line helpers.

See the Project Map for how they fit together.

docs.title: Install & downloads
docs.text: Two ways to use NodeMT5 — take our ready-made project, or take only the protocol and build your own client.

docs.title: 1 · Take our project (recommended)
docs.text:
The complete thing we built: the three layers (MT5Sugar / MT5Service / MT5Account), the TypeScript types, and the generated stubs — all wired together.

  • Just the library, for your own app:
npm install @metarpc/nodemt5

Brings the SDK, the types, and the protobuf stubs under @metarpc/nodemt5/package/.

  • The full repo (adds the runnable examples/demos/ and the tests):
git clone https://github.com/MetaRPC/NodeMT5.git
cd NodeMT5
npm install
npm run build                     # compile the TypeScript
node examples/demos/main.js 06    # run a demo (06 = sugar basics)

🎓 New here? Start with the full repo (the git clone above). It's the best way in: you get all three layers side by side (MT5Account → MT5Service → MT5Sugar) and ready-made examples written on each of them that you can run and read. Learn the SDK this way first — only once you're comfortable should you consider building your own from the raw protos (option 2 below).

docs.title: 2 · Take only the protos and build it yourself (raw gRPC)
docs.text:
For advanced use — after you know the SDK. Skip our layers and talk to the gateway from the generated stubs directly.

  • The stubs ship in the package/ folder (*_pb.js, *_grpc_pb.js). Take the whole folder, then install the runtime:
npm install google-protobuf @grpc/grpc-js
  • The raw .proto sources (to regenerate stubs for another language or version) are on the MT5 Client API Explorer → Download MT5 Protos.

⚠️ The stubs are not standalone — take the whole package/ folder, not single files. Each *_pb.js cross-requires its siblings (e.g. ./mrpc-mt5-error_pb.js), the ./google/ subfolder and google-protobuf. This path gives you raw gRPC with no 3-layer SDK — see the Protobuf Inspector.

docs.title: 🔑 API Key & Authentication
docs.text:
Connecting to the MetaRPC production endpoint (mt5.mrpc.pro:443) uses a personal API key — you get one just by registering on our site:

  1. Sign up — create a free account at https://mrpc.pro/signup.
  2. Copy your key — it's provisioned automatically; open the MT5 Client API Explorer and your key is shown at the top (Active · Copy key). Nothing to generate.
  3. Use it — pass the key to MT5Sugar.create(host, port, apiKey) (or set the MRPC_API_KEY environment variable instead of hard-coding it). In the web Explorer the key is attached to calls for you.

You'll also need an MT5 demo account (login / password / server, e.g. MetaQuotes-Demo) — see MT5 for Beginners to create one (one click for $1, or free via the MT5 terminal).

💡 TRIAL / keyless. No account yet? Pass the literal value TRIAL as the key to connect for a first look. Your own key — free from sign-up — is for normal use.

docs.title: 🆔 Session ID is automatic
docs.text: You never call GetId or supply an id header. On connect / connectEx the server generates a terminal session GUID (terminalInstanceGuid) and the SDK attaches it — alongside your API key — to every later request and stream automatically.

docs.title: Connect & read the account
docs.text:
import { MT5Sugar } from '@metarpc/nodemt5';

const sugar = MT5Sugar.create('mt5.mrpc.pro', 443, 'YOUR_API_KEY');
await sugar.quickConnect(5057947437, 'password', 'MetaQuotes-Demo');

const info = await sugar.getAccountInfo();
console.log(`${info.name} #${info.login} — ${info.balance} ${info.currency} on ${info.server}`);

Prefer environment variables? Set MT5_LOGIN / MT5_PASSWORD / MT5_SERVER and call sugar.quickConnect() with no arguments.

docs.title: A first trade (demo)
docs.text:
const ticket = await sugar.buyMarket('EURUSD', 0.01);   // tiny demo position
console.log('opened #', ticket);
await sugar.closePosition(ticket);

Trading helpers throw MrpcError on a broker rejection — wrap them in try/catch. See Return Codes & the error model.

docs.title: Dropping down a layer
docs.text:
Need something the sugar layer doesn't expose? Go down:

const service = sugar.service();   // MT5Service — typed objects
const account = sugar.account();   // MT5Account — raw protobuf

const quote = await service.getSymbolTick('EURUSD');       // Quote
const tickData = await account.symbolInfoTick(/* req */);  // raw *Data

docs.text:
• Your First Project — build a small script end to end.
  • MT5 for Beginners — the trading concepts.
  • MT5Sugar API — every helper.
  • SDK Ecosystem — how NodeMT5 pairs with the Trade Copier to mirror trades across accounts.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: The MT5, trading and SDK terms you'll meet in these docs, grouped by kind.

docs.title: 🏗️ Architectural terms
docs.text:
Three-layer architecture — the SDK is three decoupled layers, each owning the one below (sugar.service() → MT5Service, service.account() → MT5Account). See the Project Map.

MT5Account — the low-level layer. Raw gRPC: you pass protobuf *Request messages and read *Data replies with getXxx() getters. Owns the channel, the gRPC clients, auth metadata, reconnect and streaming. → overview

MT5Service — the mid layer. Same calls, but it builds the protobuf from plain arguments and returns typed objects (AccountInfo, Quote, Position…). → overview

MT5Sugar — the high layer. One-line helpers (buyMarket, closeAllPositions) with smart defaults; throws on failure. → overview

DTO — "data transfer object": the plain TypeScript interfaces MT5Service returns instead of protobuf (AccountInfo, Quote, Position, SymbolParams…).

MrpcError — the error thrown when the gateway or terminal reports a problem. Carries code, message, and for trade rejections tradeCode / tradeDescription (and mqlCode / mqlDescription); isInvalidLogin flags never-retry auth errors. Alias: MT5Error. See Return Codes → the error object.

Subscription — what a streaming method returns: { unsubscribe(): void }. Call unsubscribe() to stop the stream.

docs.title: 🧩 Node / TypeScript-specific concepts
docs.text:
Async / await — every network call returns a Promise; await it inside async functions and wrap in try/catch.

const sugar = MT5Sugar.create('mt5.mrpc.pro', 443, process.env.MRPC_API_KEY);
await sugar.quickConnect(login, 'password', 'MetaQuotes-Demo');
const balance = await sugar.getBalance();

Promise.all for parallel reads — independent calls run concurrently instead of one-by-one.

const [tick, params] = await Promise.all([
  service.getSymbolTick('EURUSD'),
  service.getSymbolParams('EURUSD'),
]);

Typed objects vs protobuf stubs — the low layer returns generated protobuf objects (reply.getXxx()); the mid layer unwraps them into typed DTOs. The stubs are typed any, so discover real names with the Protobuf Inspector.

const d = await account.openedOrders();          // low: protobuf, d.getPositionInfosList()
const { positions } = await service.getOpenedOrders(); // mid: typed Position[]

Streaming — the Subscription/callback model — a streaming method returns a Subscription and invokes your callback per payload; errors go to the optional onError. Always unsubscribe() when done. See gRPC Stream Management.

const sub = service.streamTicks(['EURUSD'], (q) => console.log(q.bid, q.ask));
// later:
sub.unsubscribe();

Connection & cleanup — connect / quickConnect opens the terminal session; disconnect(true) closes it and frees the terminal (a trial allows one per IP). Use try/finally.

try { /* … */ } finally { await sugar.service().disconnect(true); }

docs.title: Account
docs.text: Balance — closed-trade money; excludes floating P/L. Equity — balance + floating P/L; moves with open positions. Margin — funds locked to hold positions. Free margin — equity − margin; available to open more. Margin level — equity / margin × 100 (%); low levels risk a stop-out. Leverage — the multiplier (1:100) setting margin need. Trade mode — DEMO, CONTEST or REAL.

docs.title: Instruments & prices
docs.text: Symbol — a tradable instrument (EURUSD, XAUUSD). Bid / Ask — sell / buy price; spread = ask − bid. Digits — decimal places (5 for EURUSD, 3 for JPY). Tick — one price update (symbolInfoTick / onSymbolTick). DOM (Depth of Market) — the order book: pending volume at each price level.

docs.title: Orders, positions & deals (MT5 model)
docs.text: Order — an instruction to trade. Market fills now; pending (LIMIT/STOP/STOP_LIMIT) waits for a price. Position — an open trade; on MT5 distinct from the order and the deals. Deal — a single execution (fill); a position is the net of its deals. Ticket — the numeric id (a filled market order's order ticket = its position ticket). Order type (TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE): BUY=0, SELL=1, BUY_LIMIT=2, SELL_LIMIT=3, BUY_STOP=4, SELL_STOP=5, …. Position type: 0 = BUY, 1 = SELL. SL / TP — stop-loss / take-profit auto-close levels. Magic number — a client id (expertId) tagging a strategy's orders. RetCode — the trade-server return code; 10009 = DONE. See Return Codes.

docs.title: 📦 Technical concepts
docs.text:
Point — the smallest price increment (0.00001 on 5-digit EURUSD). Pip — the conventional move unit; in this SDK pip = point × (digits is 3 or 5 ? 10 : 1), so one pip on EURUSD = 0.0001. Tick value / tick size — the money value of one tick, and the price change one tick represents — inputs for P&L and sizing.

Lot / volume — trade size in lots (0.01 = micro). Must obey volume limits (volumeMin / volumeMax / volumeStep). Contract size — units of the base instrument per 1.0 lot.

Risk-based sizing — picking the lot so a stop of N pips loses a fixed % of balance: calculatePositionSize(symbol, riskPercent, stopLossPips). Risk amount = balance × riskPercent / 100. Required margin — margin a prospective order needs. Drawdown — the drop from a peak to current equity, %.

Stops level (SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL) — minimum distance, in points, SL/TP may sit from the market; closer → retcode 10016.

Trailing stop — a stop that ratchets in your favour, never back (orchestrator). Breakeven — moving the stop to entry once in profit. Hedging — holding BUY and SELL on one symbol at once (hedging accounts). Grid trading — bracketing price with pending orders (orchestrator). Scalping — many small short-lived trades. News trading — trading around releases; expect wide spreads / rejections. Kill-switch — close everything on a drawdown/margin breach (risk manager).

docs.title: 🔌 gRPC & protocol terms
docs.text:
gRPC — the RPC protocol the SDK speaks to mt5.mrpc.pro:443 (HTTP/2 + protobuf over TLS).

Protobuf — the binary message format. On the low layer you build *Request messages and read *Data replies with getXxx() getters; MT5Service hides this behind typed objects.

Streaming pattern — a server stream delivered via callback: a streaming method returns a Subscription and calls your callback per payload. See gRPC Stream Management.

Gateway — the MetaRPC service (mt5.mrpc.pro) bridging the SDK to MT5 terminals and managing sessions. Terminal — the MT5 instance your account runs on behind the gateway. Session / terminal instance guid — the id obtained on connect (ConnectEx), attached with your API key to every later call automatically. API key — your MetaRPC key; pass it to MT5Sugar.create(...), or use TRIAL.

docs.title: See also
docs.text: • Project Map · MT5 for Beginners · Getting Started · Return Codes

docs.title: gRPC Stream Management — Node
docs.text: Every live feed in NodeMT5 is a gRPC server stream. The SDK wraps each one in the same simple contract: a callback per payload, an optional error callback, and a Subscription you must cancel. This page covers the contract, the lifecycle, and how to run streams safely.

docs.title: 🧰 The Subscription contract
docs.text:
interface Subscription { unsubscribe(): void; }

Every streaming method has the shape:

method(args?, callback: (data) => void, onError?: (e: Error) => void): Subscription

const sub = account.onSymbolTick(['EURUSD'], (data) => {
  const t = data.getSymbolTick();
  console.log(t.getSymbol(), t.getBid(), t.getAsk());
}, (err) => console.error('stream error:', err.message));

// stop it later — ALWAYS do this
sub.unsubscribe();

docs.title: 🔁 What happens under the hood
docs.text:
The low-level openStream opens the gRPC server stream and forwards frames:

  • data frame → if the reply carries an error, your onError gets an MrpcError; otherwise your callback gets the reply's data.
  • transport error → onError (unless you already unsubscribed and it's a CANCELLED).
  • stream end → if you didn't cancel it, onError receives MrpcError('… stream ended').
  • unsubscribe() → cancels the gRPC call; the resulting CANCELLED is swallowed, not surfaced.

So a clean shutdown is silent, and an unexpected end is reported.

docs.title: 📡 The streams available
docs.text:
Method (MT5Account) Mapped variant (MT5Service) Payload onSymbolTick(symbols, cb) streamTicks(symbols, cb) → Quote ticks onTrade(cb) streamTradeUpdates(cb) trade events onPositionProfit(req, cb) streamPositionProfits(cb) P&L on a timer onPositionsAndPendingOrdersTickets(req, cb) streamOpenedTickets(cb) ticket snapshots on a timer onTradeTransaction(cb) streamTransactions(cb) trade transactions

streamTicks maps each tick to a friendly Quote; the others forward the raw *Data message (use its getters).

docs.title: ⏲️ Timer-driven streams
docs.text:
onPositionProfit and onPositionsAndPendingOrdersTickets push on a timer you set in the request:

import { SubscriptionsPb } from '@metarpc/nodemt5';

const req = new SubscriptionsPb.OnPositionProfitRequest();
req.setTimerPeriodMilliseconds(1000);   // every second
req.setIgnoreEmptyData(true);

const sub = account.onPositionProfit(req, (data) => {
  for (const p of data.getUpdatedPositionsList()) {
    console.log(`#${p.getTicket()} ${p.getPositionSymbol()}  ${p.getProfit()}`);
  }
});

docs.title: 🧹 Lifecycle & cleanup
docs.text:
• Keep the handle. Losing the Subscription means you can't stop the stream.
  • Unsubscribe on shutdown. Tie it to your app's teardown:
const subs = [];
subs.push(service.streamTicks(['EURUSD'], onTick));
subs.push(service.streamTradeUpdates(onTrade));

process.on('SIGINT', () => {
  subs.forEach((s) => s.unsubscribe());
  process.exit(0);
});
  • Disconnect last. After unsubscribing, await sugar.service().disconnect() to release the terminal.

docs.title: ⚠️ Backpressure & long work
docs.text: Stream callbacks run on the single event loop (Concurrency Model). If a callback does heavy synchronous work, it stalls every other callback and timer. Keep callbacks light — push data into a queue and process it elsewhere if needed. Don't await a slow unary call inside a high-frequency tick callback without guarding against overlap.

docs.title: 🔌 Reconnection
docs.text: If the terminal drops, a stream ends and onError fires. To resume: reconnect the account (sugar.quickConnect(...) / account.reconnect()) and re-subscribe. The SDK does not silently auto-resubscribe a stream — you decide the policy (immediate retry, backoff, alert).

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• MT5Account · Streaming Methods — exact payload getters.
  • Concurrency Model · Return Codes & errors.

docs.title: MT5 for Beginners
docs.text: New to MetaTrader 5? This is the 5-minute mental model you need before the code makes sense.

docs.title: What MT5 is
docs.text:
MetaTrader 5 (MT5) is a trading platform. Your account lives on a broker's server (e.g. MetaQuotes-Demo). Through it you trade symbols (instruments like EURUSD or XAUUSD).

This SDK talks to your MT5 terminal over the network (gRPC to mt5.mrpc.pro:443) so you can automate everything from Node.js.

Always learn on a demo account. It trades with fake money on real prices — no risk.

docs.title: Getting a demo account & API key
docs.text:
Registration and your API key are free. Sign up at mrpc.pro/signup and your key is provisioned automatically — nothing to generate; in the web Explorer it's even attached to every call for you. What costs money is paid usage of the service (for example the instant $1 demo below).

To run the SDK you also need an MT5 demo account (login / password / server). You can get one two ways:

docs.title: ⚡ Fastest — one click on mrpc.pro ($1)
docs.text:
Our MT5 Client API Explorer (a live API playground) spins up a demo account instantly — no terminal install:

  1. Open the MT5 Client API Explorer (sign in first). Your API key is already shown at the top (Active · Copy key).
  2. The demo server is fixed to MetaQuotes-Demo. Click Open demo account ($1). The $1 is charged to your MetaRPC balance (the account that holds your API key) — not to a broker.
  3. The demo is created instantly with a ready login / password / server — you can even run real API calls right on that page (the key is attached automatically).

Copy the demo login / password / server, then jump to Getting Started to connect from Node.

docs.title: 🖥️ Free — create a demo in the MetaTrader 5 terminal
docs.text:
The no-cost route: create a MetaQuotes demo account directly in the MT5 terminal (free), and connect with your free API key — or with the literal value TRIAL for a quick first look.

1 · Download & install MT5. Get the terminal from metatrader5.com/download and install it.

2 · Find the Navigator panel. It's on the left, below Market Watch. Its Accounts section is where you add accounts.

3 · Open a new account. Right-click Accounts → Open an account to bring up the broker-server search.

4 · Pick the MetaQuotes demo server. Find MetaQuotes-Demo (search if needed) and click Next.

5 · Choose "Open a new demo account" and click Next.

6 · Fill in the form (name, email; virtual deposit e.g. $10,000, leverage 1:100, currency USD), accept the terms, Next.

7 · Save your credentials. MT5 shows your login, password (master) and server (MetaQuotes-Demo). Copy them now — the SDK needs exactly these three values.

Two passwords are shown: the master password trades; the investor password is read-only. Use the master password with the SDK.

docs.title: The money words
docs.text:
Term In one line Balance Your settled money (no open trades counted). Equity Balance plus the profit/loss of trades you have open right now. Margin Money "reserved" while a trade is open. Free margin What's left to open new trades.

When you open a trade, equity moves tick by tick. When you close it, the result folds into balance.

docs.title: Buying and selling
docs.text:
• Buy (go long) — you profit if the price rises.
  • Sell (go short) — you profit if the price falls.

You trade in lots (volume). 0.01 is a micro lot — the smallest typical size, perfect for learning.

Two ways to enter:

  • Market order — fill now at the current price.
  • Pending order — wait for a price. A LIMIT waits for a better price; a STOP waits for a breakout.

docs.title: Protecting a trade
docs.text:
• Stop-Loss (SL) — auto-close if the price goes against you by so much. Caps the loss.
  • Take-Profit (TP) — auto-close once you've made your target.

Set them as prices, or let the SDK compute them from pip distances:

// 20-pip stop, 40-pip target, sized automatically
const lots = await sugar.calculatePositionSize('EURUSD', 1, 20);   // risk 1%
await sugar.buyMarketWithPips('EURUSD', lots, 20, 40);

docs.title: MT5's model: orders, positions, deals
docs.text:
This trips up newcomers, so remember:

  • An order is the instruction.
  • A position is the resulting open trade.
  • A deal is each execution (fill) that builds a position.

On MT5 these are separate things (unlike MT4). A filled market BUY gives you a position, identified by a ticket.

docs.title: Your first 10 lines
docs.text:
import { MT5Sugar } from '@metarpc/nodemt5';

const sugar = MT5Sugar.create('mt5.mrpc.pro', 443);
await sugar.quickConnect(login, 'password', 'MetaQuotes-Demo');

console.log('balance', await sugar.getBalance());
const ticket = await sugar.buyMarket('EURUSD', 0.01);   // tiny demo trade
await sugar.closePosition(ticket);

Layer Source What it does Overview 3 · MT5Sugar src/MT5Sugar.ts One-line helpers: buyMarket, closeAllPositions, risk-based sizing, pip SL/TP, daily stats. 12 groups. MT5Service overview 1 · MT5Account src/MT5Account.ts Low-level gRPC: protobuf request/reply, connect/session, reconnect, streaming. Everything builds on it. 7 groups. MT5Account overview

docs.title: Protobuf Inspector Guide — Node
docs.text:
The generated package/*_pb.js stubs are typed any, so TypeScript can't tell you a message's real getters, setters or enum names. This guide shows how to discover them at runtime — the fastest way to avoid "x.setPrice is not a function" surprises.

🛠️ Ready-made tool. The repo ships a runnable inspector — no need to write the snippets yourself:

node examples/demos/helpers/17_protobuf_inspector.js                       # interactive REPL
node examples/demos/helpers/17_protobuf_inspector.js OrderCalcMarginRequest # one-shot: getters/setters
node examples/demos/helpers/17_protobuf_inspector.js enum MqlErrorTradeCode # one-shot: enum values
node examples/demos/helpers/17_protobuf_inspector.js search Tick            # find message/enum names

It's offline (loads the stubs only — no connection, no key). REPL commands: list · <TypeName> · search <text> · enum <Name> · stats · help · exit. The techniques below are what it does under the hood.

docs.title: 🎯 Why you need it
docs.text:
• Field accessors aren't guessable. Repeated fields append List (getPositionInfosList); some getters are oddly cased (getTradetickvalue, not getTradeTickValue).
  • Request setters vary. OrderCalcMarginRequest uses setOpenPrice, not setPrice.
  • Enum namespaces surprise. SymbolInfoDoubleProperty, MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode with MRPC_-prefixed values.
  • any typing hides all of it. The only source of truth is the stub — inspect it.

docs.title: 🔍 List a message's getters / setters
docs.text:
// node -e "...": print every getter of a message type
const Pb = require('@metarpc/nodemt5/package/mt5-term-api-trade-functions_pb');

const getters = Object.getOwnPropertyNames(Pb.OrderCalcMarginData.prototype)
  .filter((n) => n.startsWith('get'));
const setters = Object.getOwnPropertyNames(Pb.OrderCalcMarginRequest.prototype)
  .filter((n) => n.startsWith('set'));

console.log('getters:', getters.join(' '));
console.log('setters:', setters.join(' '));

Tip: the SDK re-exports these modules too — require('@metarpc/nodemt5').TradeFunctionsPb is the same object.

docs.title: 🧱 Find a message type by name
docs.text:
const Pb = require('@metarpc/nodemt5').SubscriptionsPb;

// which message types mention "Tick"?
console.log(Object.keys(Pb).filter((k) => /Tick/.test(k)));
// → [ 'OnSymbolTickData', 'OnSymbolTickReply', 'OnSymbolTickRequest', 'MrpcSubscriptionMqlTick', ... ]

Then inspect the one you want with the getter/setter trick above.

docs.title: 🎛️ List an enum's values
docs.text:
const { MarketInfoPb } = require('@metarpc/nodemt5');

console.log(Object.keys(MarketInfoPb.SymbolInfoDoubleProperty).slice(0, 10));
// → [ 'SYMBOL_BID', 'SYMBOL_BIDHIGH', 'SYMBOL_BIDLOW', 'SYMBOL_POINT', ... ]

console.log(MarketInfoPb.SymbolInfoIntegerProperty.SYMBOL_DIGITS);  // the number

To find which namespace holds an enum:

const mi = require('@metarpc/nodemt5').MarketInfoPb;
console.log(Object.keys(mi).filter((k) => /Property|Enum/.test(k)));

docs.title: 🧪 Inspect a live reply
docs.text:
Log what the server actually returned — handy when a getter comes back empty:

const data = await account.accountSummary();
console.log(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(Object.getPrototypeOf(data))
  .filter((n) => n.startsWith('get')));
console.log('balance:', data.getAccountBalance());

A reply message also serialises to an array: data.toObject() (where available) or data.serializeBinary() for the raw bytes.

docs.title: 🗺️ Where each service lives
docs.text: Package stub Holds mt5-term-api-connection_pb connect / disconnect / getId mt5-term-api-account-helper_pb account summary, symbol params, tick value mt5-term-api-account-information_pb AccountInfo* property enums mt5-term-api-market-info_pb symbol info, sessions, DOM, SymbolInfo*Property enums mt5-term-api-trading-helper_pb orderSend/modify/close, TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE mt5-term-api-trade-functions_pb orderCheck / orderCalc* mt5-term-api-subscriptions_pb the On* streams

docs.title: ✅ A quick workflow
docs.text:
1. Suspect a wrong accessor? List the message's getters/setters.
  2. Copy the exact name into your code.
  3. Re-run — runtime confirms it.

This is exactly how the SDK's own methods were verified against the stubs.

docs.title: What is a RetCode?
docs.text:
A RetCode (return code) is the status the MT5 trade server returns after a trading operation. It tells you success, or the exact reason for a failure (insufficient margin, invalid price, market closed…).

RetCodes appear only in trading methods — opening, modifying and closing orders — because only those go through the broker and can be rejected.

docs.title: 📌 Source
docs.text:
RetCodes are standard MQL5 codes — identical across every language (Node.js, Python, C#, Go…) and returned straight from the trade server. See the MQL5 reference: Trade Server Return Codes (ENUM_TRADE_RETCODE).

10009 = TRADE_RETCODE_DONE = success.

docs.title: Where a RetCode reaches you
docs.text:
It arrives one of two ways — handle both:

  1. In the reply. placeOrder / modifyOrder / closeOrder resolve with a result whose retcode field carries it:
const r = await service.placeOrder({ action: 'BUY', symbol: 'EURUSD', volume: 0.10 });
if (r.retcode === 10009) console.log('done, ticket', r.ticket);
else console.log('rejected:', r.retcode, r.retcodeDescription);
  1. As a thrown MrpcError. A request the terminal refuses outright (e.g. an invalid volume) rejects the promise with an MrpcError (see the error object below) whose tradeCode / tradeDescription carry the RetCode:
import { MrpcError } from '@metarpc/nodemt5';

try {
  await account.orderSend(req);
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof MrpcError && e.tradeCode) {
    console.log('trade code:', e.tradeCode, e.tradeDescription);
  } else {
    throw e;   // transport / gateway error
  }
}

The high-level MT5Sugar trading helpers throw on any non-10009 retcode, so there you only try/catch.

docs.title: 🧯 The error object — MrpcError
docs.text:
A trade rejection and a gateway/terminal error both surface as MrpcError (exported alias MT5Error); a pure transport failure throws the gRPC error instead.

Field Description code error code — TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND, or a retcode like 10018. message human-readable ("<code>: <message>"). error the raw reply error object (absent for a transport failure or a sugar-layer rejection). mqlCode / mqlDescription the terminal's MQL error, when the terminal refused. tradeCode / tradeDescription the trade server's RetCode of a refused order. isInvalidLogin true for INVALID_LOGIN / WRONG_PASSWORD / INVALID_ACCOUNT — never retry these.

NotConnectedError (code NOT_CONNECTED) is a subclass thrown when you call a method before connect() succeeds.

import { MrpcError } from '@metarpc/nodemt5';

try {
  await service.placeOrder({ symbol: 'EURUSD', action: 'BUY', volume: 0.01 });
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof MrpcError) {
    console.log(e.code, e.message);          // e.g. "10018", "...: Market is closed"
    console.log(e.tradeCode, e.mqlCode);     // decoded codes when present
  } else throw e;                            // transport failure
}

Codes you'll meet: TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND (reconnect) · MQL5_SIDE_TRADE_ERROR (read tradeCode) · NOT_CONNECTED (connect first) · INVALID_LOGIN / WRONG_PASSWORD (don't retry) · plus the trade retcodes below.

docs.title: ✅ Success codes
docs.text: Code Name Meaning Example 10009 TRADE_RETCODE_DONE Completed successfully Market order opened/closed 10010 TRADE_RETCODE_DONE_PARTIAL Partial execution Only part of the volume filled 10008 TRADE_RETCODE_PLACED Pending order placed Limit/Stop order placed

docs.title: 🔁 Requote / price moved — retry
docs.text: Code Name Meaning 10004 TRADE_RETCODE_REQUOTE Price changed, retry 10020 TRADE_RETCODE_PRICE_CHANGED Price changed, retry

docs.title: 🧾 Validation — fix the request
docs.text: Code Name Meaning 10013 TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID Invalid request / parameters 10014 TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID_VOLUME Volume below min or above max 10015 TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID_PRICE Price doesn't match symbol rules 10016 TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID_STOPS SL/TP too close (check SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL) 10022 TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID_EXPIRATION Bad expiration time 10030 TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID_FILL Filling type not allowed 10035 TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID_ORDER Order type prohibited for symbol 10038 TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID_CLOSE_VOLUME Close volume exceeds position

docs.title: 🚫 Restrictions — check trading conditions
docs.text: Code Name Meaning 10017 TRADE_RETCODE_TRADE_DISABLED Trading disabled for the symbol 10018 TRADE_RETCODE_MARKET_CLOSED Outside trading hours 10026 TRADE_RETCODE_SERVER_DISABLES_AT Auto-trading disabled by server 10027 TRADE_RETCODE_CLIENT_DISABLES_AT Auto-trading disabled by terminal 10032 TRADE_RETCODE_ONLY_REAL Unavailable on demo 10042 TRADE_RETCODE_LONG_ONLY Only long allowed 10043 TRADE_RETCODE_SHORT_ONLY Only short allowed 10044 TRADE_RETCODE_CLOSE_ONLY Only closing allowed 10045 TRADE_RETCODE_FIFO_CLOSE Must close by FIFO 10046 TRADE_RETCODE_HEDGE_PROHIBITED Hedging disabled

docs.title: 💸 Limits — reduce volume / positions
docs.text: Code Name Meaning 10019 TRADE_RETCODE_NO_MONEY Insufficient funds — check free margin 10033 TRADE_RETCODE_LIMIT_ORDERS Pending-orders limit reached 10034 TRADE_RETCODE_LIMIT_VOLUME Volume limit reached 10040 TRADE_RETCODE_LIMIT_POSITIONS Positions limit reached

docs.title: ⏳ Temporary — retry with a delay
docs.text: Code Name Meaning Retry? 10011 TRADE_RETCODE_ERROR Processing error No 10012 TRADE_RETCODE_TIMEOUT Request timeout Yes 10021 TRADE_RETCODE_NO_QUOTES No quotes Yes 10024 TRADE_RETCODE_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS Rate limited Yes (with delay) 10028 TRADE_RETCODE_LOCKED Locked for processing Yes 10029 TRADE_RETCODE_FROZEN Order/position frozen Yes 10031 TRADE_RETCODE_CONNECTION No connection Yes

docs.title: 🔃 State
docs.text: Code Name Meaning 10023 TRADE_RETCODE_ORDER_CHANGED Order state changed 10025 TRADE_RETCODE_NO_CHANGES New params equal current 10036 TRADE_RETCODE_POSITION_CLOSED Position no longer exists 10039 TRADE_RETCODE_CLOSE_ORDER_EXIST A close order already exists

docs.title: ❌ Rejected / cancelled
docs.text: Code Name Meaning 10006 TRADE_RETCODE_REJECT Broker rejected 10007 TRADE_RETCODE_CANCEL Cancelled by trader 10041 TRADE_RETCODE_REJECT_CANCEL Pending activation rejected & cancelled

docs.title: The MetaRPC SDK family
docs.text:
Where NodeMT5 sits — and how it pairs with the Trade Copier to mirror a strategy across accounts.

MetaRPC ships two families of SDKs. They share the same authentication (ApiKey + owner user_key), the same gRPC-over-TLS transport to *.mrpc.pro, the same mrpc.pro portal and the same $1 demo onboarding — but they do different jobs.

Family Job Endpoint SDKs Terminal SDKs operate one trading account — connect, read, trade, stream mt5.mrpc.pro:443 (MT5) NodeMT5, GoMT5, CSharpMT5, CppMT5, JavaMT5, PyMT5 (+ MT4 variants) Copier SDKs mirror trades between accounts (master → followers) copy.mrpc.pro:443 NodeCopier, GoCopier, CSharpCopier, PyCopier, …

NodeMT5 is a Terminal SDK. When you want to replicate what happens on one account to others, reach for the Copier SDK — in Node that's NodeCopier (@metarpc/nodecopier).

docs.title: How NodeMT5 and NodeCopier relate
docs.text:
NodeMT5 (this SDK) NodeCopier Scope one account a master → follower pair Does connect, quotes, placeOrder, streams start · list · pause · remove a copier Endpoint mt5.mrpc.pro:443 copy.mrpc.pro:443 Thinks in ticks, orders, positions risk sizing, pause/resume, copy logs

One sentence: NodeMT5 is where trades are produced and observed on an account; NodeCopier is how they're distributed to followers.

docs.title: The bridge — a shared terminal session
docs.text:
A copier's account carries an optional id — a terminal session GUID. That's exactly the value NodeMT5 obtains on connect: after connect / connectEx, the session GUID (terminalInstanceGuid) lives on account().id. So an account you're already running with NodeMT5 can be enrolled into a copier without reconnecting.

NodeCopier also understands MT5 account types MT5 and MT5_MRPC (plus MT4, cTrader CT, TradeLocker TL) — the same MRPC-hosted terminals NodeMT5 drives.

docs.title: End-to-end: run a strategy on the master, replicate to a follower
docs.text:
import { MT5Sugar } from '@metarpc/nodemt5';
import { CopierSugar } from '@metarpc/nodecopier';

const KEY = process.env.MRPC_API_KEY;   // owner key — note: TRIAL is NOT an owner key for the copier

// 1 · Operate the MASTER account with NodeMT5
const master = MT5Sugar.create('mt5.mrpc.pro', 443, KEY);
await master.quickConnect(Number(process.env.MASTER_LOGIN), process.env.MASTER_PASSWORD!, 'MetaQuotes-Demo');
const masterSessionId = master.account().id;   // the ConnectEx terminal GUID → copier Account.id

// 2 · Start a copier: MASTER → FOLLOWER (NodeCopier, on copy.mrpc.pro)
await CopierSugar.create()
  .withCredentials(KEY!)
  .fromMaster({ type: 'MT5', user: Number(process.env.MASTER_LOGIN), password: process.env.MASTER_PASSWORD!, server: 'MetaQuotes-Demo', id: masterSessionId! })
  .toSlave({ type: 'MT5', user: Number(process.env.SLAVE_LOGIN), password: process.env.SLAVE_PASSWORD!, server: 'MetaQuotes-Demo' })
  .withLotMultiplier(1.0)   // or .withFixedLot(0.1)
  .withCopySl(true).withCopyTp(true)
  .start();

// 3 · Trades you now place on the master via NodeMT5 replicate to the follower
const ticket = await master.buyMarket('EURUSD', 0.01);
// … the copier mirrors the open (and the later close) onto the follower account

Install: npm install @metarpc/nodecopier alongside @metarpc/nodemt5.

Risk sizing (the copier's riskType): FixedLot · LotMultiplier · BalanceMultiplier · FixedBalanceMultiplier · EquityMultiplier. Plus copySl / copyTp / copyPendingOrders / reverseCopy.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & gotchas
docs.text:
• Two services, two endpoints. NodeMT5 talks to mt5.mrpc.pro; NodeCopier to copy.mrpc.pro. The copier is a companion service, not a replacement.
  • Owner key required for the copier. TRIAL works for a first look on a terminal, but the copier needs a real owner user_key.
  • Transport success ≠ broker execution. A successful start means the copier was created — confirm the follower actually opened the trade (NodeCopier's trade logs, or read the follower with NodeMT5's getOpenedOrders).
  • Demo-first. Use disposable demo accounts for copier tests. Hosted terminals and running copiers are billed separately (see pricing).

docs.title: Usercode Sandbox Guide — Node
docs.text: examples/demos/usercode/18_usercode.js is a ready-to-edit scratchpad. It hands you an already-connected MT5Sugar exposing all three layers, so you can try the SDK without writing any connection or menu plumbing.

docs.title: 🚀 Run it
docs.text:
node examples/demos/main.js 18

Credentials come from examples/demos/config/config.json or the env vars MT5_LOGIN / MT5_PASSWORD / MT5_SERVER / MRPC_API_KEY (leave the key empty for trial access).

docs.title: 🧱 What you get
docs.text:
module.exports = async function demo(sugar, cfg) {
  // sugar : a connected MT5Sugar
  //   sugar.service()  → MT5Service (typed objects)
  //   sugar.account()  → MT5Account (raw protobuf)
  // cfg   : { testSymbol, testVolume, user, server, ... }

  //  YOUR CODE HERE — sugar is already connected.
};

All three layers are one call away — reach for whichever altitude fits:

// high level — one-liners
console.log('balance', await sugar.getBalance());
console.log('bid', await sugar.getBid(cfg.testSymbol));

// mid level — typed objects
const acc = await sugar.service().getAccountSummary();
console.log(acc.equity, acc.currency);

// low level — raw protobuf
const data = await sugar.account().accountSummary();
console.log(data.getAccountBalance());

docs.title: 🧪 Good first experiments
docs.text:
Inspect your account & market (read-only):

console.log(`balance ${(await sugar.getBalance()).toFixed(2)}  equity ${(await sugar.getEquity()).toFixed(2)}`);
const p = await sugar.getPriceInfo(cfg.testSymbol);
console.log(`${cfg.testSymbol}  ${p.bid}/${p.ask}  ${p.spreadPips.toFixed(1)} pips`);

for (const pos of await sugar.getOpenPositions()) {
  console.log(`#${pos.ticket} ${pos.symbol} ${pos.volume} P/L ${pos.profit.toFixed(2)}`);
}

Size a trade by risk (still no order sent):

const lots = await sugar.calculatePositionSize(cfg.testSymbol, 1, 20);   // 1% over 20 pips
const { ok, reason } = await sugar.canOpenPosition(cfg.testSymbol, lots);
console.log('would open', lots, 'lots →', ok ? 'OK' : reason);

Stream a few ticks:

await new Promise((resolve) => {
  let n = 0;
  const sub = sugar.service().streamTicks([cfg.testSymbol], (q) => {
    console.log(q.bid, q.ask);
    if (++n >= 5) { sub.unsubscribe(); resolve(); }
  });
});

docs.title: ⚠️ Trading from the sandbox
docs.text:
Nothing trades until you call a trading method. When you do, keep it small and on the demo account:

const ticket = await sugar.buyMarket(cfg.testSymbol, cfg.testVolume);   // tiny demo order
await sugar.closePosition(ticket);

Trading one-liners throw on a broker rejection (e.g. 10018 market closed) — wrap them in try/catch. See Return Codes.

docs.title: 💡 Tips
docs.text:
• Use the Protobuf Inspector snippets here to discover accessors live.
  • The sandbox disconnects for you when the demo returns — no cleanup needed.
  • Copy a working snippet into your own project once it does what you want.

docs.title: Your First Project
docs.text: Build a small, complete NodeMT5 script: connect, quote, trade with risk sizing, and report.

docs.title: 1 · Set up
docs.text:
mkdir mt5-bot && cd mt5-bot
npm init -y
npm install @metarpc/nodemt5

Create index.mjs.

docs.title: 2 · Connect
docs.text:
import { MT5Sugar } from '@metarpc/nodemt5';

const sugar = MT5Sugar.create('mt5.mrpc.pro', 443, process.env.MRPC_API_KEY);
await sugar.quickConnect(
  Number(process.env.MT5_LOGIN),
  process.env.MT5_PASSWORD,
  process.env.MT5_SERVER,         // e.g. MetaQuotes-Demo
);
console.log('connected?', sugar.isConnected());

Need the MRPC_API_KEY? Register at https://mrpc.pro/signup — your key is then provisioned automatically and shown in the MT5 Client API Explorer (Copy key). See Getting Started → API Key. (Or omit it for keyless TRIAL access while testing.)

docs.title: 3 · Look at the market
docs.text:
const symbol = 'EURUSD';
const price = await sugar.getPriceInfo(symbol);
console.log(`${symbol}  bid ${price.bid}  ask ${price.ask}  ${price.spreadPips.toFixed(1)} pips`);

docs.title: 4 · Trade with risk sizing
docs.text:
// risk 1% of balance over a 20-pip stop, 40-pip target
const lots = await sugar.calculatePositionSize(symbol, 1, 20);

const { ok, reason } = await sugar.canOpenPosition(symbol, lots);
if (!ok) throw new Error('cannot trade: ' + reason);

const ticket = await sugar.buyMarketWithPips(symbol, lots, 20, 40);
console.log('opened #', ticket, 'with', lots, 'lots');

docs.title: 5 · Manage & report
docs.text:
console.log('open positions:', await sugar.countOpenPositions());
console.log('floating P/L:', await sugar.getTotalProfit());

// tidy up for the demo
await sugar.closeAllPositions();

const stats = await sugar.getDailyStats();
console.log(`today: ${stats.totalDeals} deals, net ${stats.totalProfit.toFixed(2)}`);

docs.title: 6 · Run it
docs.text:
MT5_LOGIN=5057947437 MT5_PASSWORD=secret MT5_SERVER=MetaQuotes-Demo \
MRPC_API_KEY=YOUR_KEY node index.mjs

docs.title: MT5Account — Master Overview
docs.text:
One page to orient fast: what lives where, how to choose the right API, and jump links to every overview and method spec in this docs set.

metarpc.MT5Account (from @metarpc/nodemt5) is the low-level layer — a thin, 1:1-with-the-wire client. Each method maps to a single gRPC RPC: you pass a generated protobuf *Request and get back the reply's *Data payload, or it rejects with an MrpcError. It owns the gRPC channel, the seven service clients, the auth metadata (apikey + terminal id) and the connection lifecycle.

import { MT5Account } from '@metarpc/nodemt5';

When to use this layer

Use MT5Account when you need a field the friendly layers do not expose, or full control over the exact request. For everyday work prefer MT5Service (plain args + typed objects) or MT5Sugar (one-liners).

docs.title: 🔌 Usage pattern (raw gRPC)
docs.text:
Every method is called on an MT5Account. It owns the gRPC channel, sends the terminal id and API key as metadata, and unwraps the reply — returning the protobuf *Data payload or rejecting with an error.

import { MT5Account } from '@metarpc/nodemt5';
const pb = MT5Account; // the generated *Pb bindings are exported from the module

// Create the client (prepares the gRPC channel; apiKey from MRPC_API_KEY, else TRIAL)
const account = new MT5Account('mt5.mrpc.pro', 443);

// Connect the terminal (ConnectEx by broker server name)
await account.connect({ user: 5057947437, password: 'password', server: 'MetaQuotes-Demo' });
// The gateway returns a terminal session GUID; later calls reuse it automatically.

// Call a method: returns the Data payload, or throws MrpcError / a transport error
const s = await account.accountSummary();
console.log('Balance:', s.getAccountBalance(), s.getAccountCurrency());

Every method follows the same shape:

  • Proto Service/Method: Service.Method(Request) → Reply
  • Client call: account.method(req?) resolves with the *Data payload.
  • Reply structure: the reply carries either a data payload or an error; MT5Account returns the data and turns error into a thrown MrpcError.
  • Errors are exceptions — there are no error return values; await inside try/catch.

Timestamps: proto uses google.protobuf.Timestamp (or raw unix seconds on some messages); read .getSeconds(). The friendly MT5Service layer converts these to numbers / UTC for you.

Streaming methods: return a { unsubscribe() } handle. The SDK reads the stream and invokes your callback for each payload; call unsubscribe() to stop.

docs.title: Layer 1: MT5Account (Low-Level) — You are here!
docs.text:
What: direct protobuf/gRPC communication with the MT5 terminal. Works with protobuf *Request / *Data objects; raw gRPC calls; complete access to every MT5 function; highest complexity.

Location: src/MT5Account.ts

docs.title: Layer 2: MT5Service
docs.text: What: a friendly facade over MT5Account — plain arguments and typed objects (AccountInfo, Quote, Position…). No protobuf. Location: src/MT5Service.ts → overview.

docs.title: Layer 3: MT5Sugar
docs.text:
What: high-level convenience API — one-liners, risk-based position sizing, smart defaults. Location: src/MT5Sugar.ts → overview.

Each layer owns the one below it: MT5Sugar owns an MT5Service, which owns an MT5Account. From Sugar you can always reach down with sugar.service() and sugar.account().

docs.title: 💡 Key concepts
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions. A server-side rejection throws metarpc.MrpcError (carrying mqlCode / tradeCode); a transport failure throws the gRPC error. There are no error return values.
  • Session id is automatic. connect() (ConnectEx) obtains a terminal session GUID; the SDK attaches it (+ your apikey) to every later call and stream. You never call GetId manually.
  • Trade retcode. orderSend / orderClose carry a trade-server result code — 10009 = DONE (success). See Return Codes.
  • MT5 has positions. Unlike MT4, MT5 separates positions (net market exposure), orders (pending/working) and deals (executed transactions in history).

"Trade safe, code clean, and may your gRPC streams always flow smoothly."

docs.title: 📊 Getting Account Double Properties
docs.text:
Request: one floating-point account property (AccountInfoDoubleData → a number) from MT5 — balance, equity, profit, margin figures, and more, selected by an enum.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account.accountInfoDouble(...) (from @metarpc/nodemt5)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.AccountInformation
  • Proto definition: AccountInfoDouble (in mt5-term-api-account-information.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.AccountInformation
  • Method: AccountInfoDouble(AccountInfoDoubleRequest) → AccountInfoDoubleReply
  • Low-level client (generated): AccountInformationClient.accountInfoDouble(request, metadata, opts)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC that returns a single double account property, chosen by an AccountInfoDoublePropertyType value.
  • Why you need it. Read exactly the number you care about (e.g. ACCOUNT_EQUITY) without pulling the whole AccountSummary.
  • Sanity check. ACCOUNT_BALANCE returns a positive number on a funded account.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use it when you want one precise figure, cheaply:

  • A live equity or free-margin readout for a dashboard.
  • A margin-level gate right before placing a trade.
  • Polling a single metric on a timer without the overhead of the full summary.

docs.title: 📚 Tutorial
docs.text:
A typical call, step by step:

  1. Connect so the SDK has a terminal session (sugar.quickConnect(...) or account.connect(...)).
  2. Pick the property from the AccountInfoDoublePropertyType enum, e.g. ACCOUNT_EQUITY.
  3. Call account.accountInfoDouble(propertyId) — it builds the protobuf request, sends it, and unwraps the reply's getRequestedValue() for you.
  4. Use the number — it's a plain number, already in the account's deposit currency.
import { MT5Account, AccountInformationPb } from '@metarpc/nodemt5';
const P = AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoDoublePropertyType;

const equity = await account.accountInfoDouble(P.ACCOUNT_EQUITY);

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
import { MT5Account, AccountInformationPb } from '@metarpc/nodemt5';

class MT5Account {
  // Read one ACCOUNT_* double property. Pass an AccountInfoDoublePropertyType value.
  // Returns the value already unwrapped from AccountInfoDoubleData.getRequestedValue().
  accountInfoDouble(propertyId: number, timeoutMs?: number): Promise<number>;
}

Request message:

AccountInfoDoubleRequest { AccountInfoDoublePropertyType property_id = 1; }

Reply message:

AccountInfoDoubleReply {
  oneof response {
    AccountInfoDoubleData data = 1;   // getRequestedValue(): double
    Error error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text:
Parameter Type Description propertyId number (AccountInfoDoublePropertyType) Which double property to read. timeoutMs number? Optional per-call deadline (defaults to the SDK's 15 s).

The low-level method takes the enum value directly — there's no request object to build by hand. For plain arguments at the mid layer, see MT5Service.getAccountDouble.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — AccountInfoDoubleData
docs.text: Field JS accessor Type Description requested value getRequestedValue() number The property's value. The SDK returns this directly.

docs.title: 🧱 Related enums (from proto)
docs.text: 💡 Enum usage. In Node these are namespace objects — access a value as AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoDoublePropertyType.ACCOUNT_EQUITY (a number).

docs.title: AccountInfoDoublePropertyType
docs.text: Constant Meaning ACCOUNT_BALANCE Balance (excludes floating P/L). ACCOUNT_CREDIT Credit. ACCOUNT_PROFIT Current floating profit of all open positions. ACCOUNT_EQUITY Equity = balance + floating P/L. ACCOUNT_MARGIN Margin used by open positions. ACCOUNT_MARGIN_FREE Free margin for new positions. ACCOUNT_MARGIN_LEVEL Margin level, percent (equity / margin × 100). ACCOUNT_MARGIN_SO_CALL Margin call level. ACCOUNT_MARGIN_SO_SO Stop-out level. ACCOUNT_MARGIN_INITIAL Reserved initial margin. ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MAINTENANCE Reserved maintenance margin. ACCOUNT_ASSETS Current assets. ACCOUNT_LIABILITIES Current liabilities. ACCOUNT_COMMISSION_BLOCKED Blocked commission.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• One value per call. For many figures at once prefer AccountSummary — it returns them all in a single RPC.
  • Currency. All these doubles are in the account's deposit currency (read via AccountInfoString ACCOUNT_CURRENCY).
  • Margin level is 0 when flat. With no open positions ACCOUNT_MARGIN is 0, so ACCOUNT_MARGIN_LEVEL reads 0 — don't treat that as "danger".
  • Errors are exceptions. A gateway/terminal failure rejects the promise with an MrpcError.

docs.title: 1) Get account balance
docs.text:
import { MT5Account, AccountInformationPb } from '@metarpc/nodemt5';
const P = AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoDoublePropertyType;

const balance = await account.accountInfoDouble(P.ACCOUNT_BALANCE);
console.log('balance:', balance.toFixed(2));

docs.title: 2) Get current equity
docs.text:
const equity = await account.accountInfoDouble(P.ACCOUNT_EQUITY);
console.log('equity:', equity.toFixed(2));

docs.title: 3) Check margin level before trading
docs.text:
const level = await account.accountInfoDouble(P.ACCOUNT_MARGIN_LEVEL);
if (level !== 0 && level < 200) {
  console.warn(`margin level ${level.toFixed(0)}% — too low to add risk`);
}

docs.title: 4) Free margin available
docs.text:
const free = await account.accountInfoDouble(P.ACCOUNT_MARGIN_FREE);
console.log('free margin:', free.toFixed(2));

docs.title: 5) Floating profit / loss
docs.text:
const profit = await account.accountInfoDouble(P.ACCOUNT_PROFIT);
console.log(profit >= 0 ? `in profit +${profit.toFixed(2)}` : `drawdown ${profit.toFixed(2)}`);

docs.title: 6) Read several properties at once
docs.text:
const P = AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoDoublePropertyType;
const [balance, equity, free, level] = await Promise.all([
  account.accountInfoDouble(P.ACCOUNT_BALANCE),
  account.accountInfoDouble(P.ACCOUNT_EQUITY),
  account.accountInfoDouble(P.ACCOUNT_MARGIN_FREE),
  account.accountInfoDouble(P.ACCOUNT_MARGIN_LEVEL),
]);
console.log({ balance, equity, free, level });

Running them with Promise.all sends the calls concurrently — see Concurrency Model.

docs.title: Pre-trade funding check
docs.text:
async function canAfford(account: MT5Account, requiredMargin: number): Promise<boolean> {
  const P = AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoDoublePropertyType;
  const free = await account.accountInfoDouble(P.ACCOUNT_MARGIN_FREE);
  return free >= requiredMargin;
}

docs.title: Margin-level warning
docs.text:
async function marginWarning(account: MT5Account): Promise<string | null> {
  const P = AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoDoublePropertyType;
  const level = await account.accountInfoDouble(P.ACCOUNT_MARGIN_LEVEL);
  if (level === 0) return null;                 // flat
  if (level < 100) return `CRITICAL ${level.toFixed(0)}%`;
  if (level < 200) return `low ${level.toFixed(0)}%`;
  return null;
}

docs.title: 🔢 Getting Account Integer Properties
docs.text:
Request: one integer account property (AccountInfoIntegerData → a number) from MT5 — login, leverage, trade mode, and the trade/hedge flags, selected by an enum.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account.accountInfoInteger(...) (from @metarpc/nodemt5)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.AccountInformation
  • Proto definition: AccountInfoInteger (in mt5-term-api-account-information.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.AccountInformation
  • Method: AccountInfoInteger(AccountInfoIntegerRequest) → AccountInfoIntegerReply
  • Low-level client (generated): AccountInformationClient.accountInfoInteger(request, metadata, opts)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC that returns a single integer/flag account property, chosen by an AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType value.
  • Why you need it. Read ACCOUNT_LEVERAGE, the trade mode, or a boolean flag like ACCOUNT_TRADE_ALLOWED without the full AccountSummary.
  • Sanity check. ACCOUNT_LOGIN returns your account number.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use it to read account identity, configuration and permission flags:

  • The account login and leverage.
  • Whether trading / Expert Advisors are allowed right now.
  • The margin mode (netting vs hedging) and FIFO / hedge rules.

docs.title: 📚 Tutorial
docs.text:
1. Connect so the SDK has a terminal session.
  2. Pick the property from AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType, e.g. ACCOUNT_LEVERAGE.
  3. Call account.accountInfoInteger(propertyId) — it builds the request, sends it, and unwraps getRequestedValue() (coerced to a JS number).
  4. Interpret booleans as 1 = true / 0 = false, and enums (trade mode, margin mode) against their enum tables.
import { MT5Account, AccountInformationPb } from '@metarpc/nodemt5';
const P = AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType;

const leverage = await account.accountInfoInteger(P.ACCOUNT_LEVERAGE);   // e.g. 100
const canTrade = (await account.accountInfoInteger(P.ACCOUNT_TRADE_ALLOWED)) === 1;

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
import { MT5Account, AccountInformationPb } from '@metarpc/nodemt5';

class MT5Account {
  // Read one ACCOUNT_* integer property. Pass an AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType value.
  // Returns getRequestedValue() coerced to a JS number.
  accountInfoInteger(propertyId: number, timeoutMs?: number): Promise<number>;
}

Request message:

AccountInfoIntegerRequest { AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType property_id = 1; }

Reply message:

AccountInfoIntegerReply {
  oneof response {
    AccountInfoIntegerData data = 1;   // getRequestedValue(): int64
    Error error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description propertyId number (AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType) Which integer property to read. timeoutMs number? Optional per-call deadline (default 15 s).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — AccountInfoIntegerData
docs.text:
Field JS accessor Type Description requested value getRequestedValue() number The property's value. Returned directly, coerced to number.

The proto type is int64; the SDK coerces it with Number(...). ACCOUNT_LOGIN fits safely in a JS number.

docs.title: 🧱 Related enums (from proto)
docs.text: Access as AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType.ACCOUNT_LEVERAGE (a number).

docs.title: AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType
docs.text: Constant Meaning ACCOUNT_LOGIN Account number (ID). ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE 0 = DEMO, 1 = CONTEST, 2 = REAL (see AccountSummary). ACCOUNT_LEVERAGE Leverage, e.g. 100 for 1:100. ACCOUNT_LIMIT_ORDERS Max allowed pending orders. ACCOUNT_MARGIN_SO_MODE Stop-out mode (percent vs money). ACCOUNT_TRADE_ALLOWED 1 if trading is allowed for the account. ACCOUNT_TRADE_EXPERT 1 if automated (EA) trading is allowed. ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE 0 = RETAIL_NETTING, 1 = EXCHANGE, 2 = RETAIL_HEDGING. ACCOUNT_CURRENCY_DIGITS Decimal places of the deposit currency. ACCOUNT_FIFO_CLOSE 1 if positions must be closed FIFO. ACCOUNT_HEDGE_ALLOWED 1 if opposite positions per symbol are allowed.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Booleans are 0/1. Compare === 1 for the *_ALLOWED / *_CLOSE flags.
  • Enums come back as numbers. Map ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE / ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE against their tables (or use AccountSummary which maps trade mode to a string).
  • For everything at once, AccountSummary already carries login, leverage, trade mode, margin mode and the flags.

docs.title: 1) Account login & leverage
docs.text:
import { MT5Account, AccountInformationPb } from '@metarpc/nodemt5';
const P = AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType;

const login = await account.accountInfoInteger(P.ACCOUNT_LOGIN);
const leverage = await account.accountInfoInteger(P.ACCOUNT_LEVERAGE);
console.log(`#${login}  leverage 1:${leverage}`);

docs.title: 2) Is trading allowed right now?
docs.text:
const allowed = (await account.accountInfoInteger(P.ACCOUNT_TRADE_ALLOWED)) === 1;
const expert  = (await account.accountInfoInteger(P.ACCOUNT_TRADE_EXPERT))  === 1;
if (!allowed) console.warn('account trading disabled');
if (!expert)  console.warn('automated trading disabled');

docs.title: 3) Hedging or netting?
docs.text:
const mode = await account.accountInfoInteger(P.ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE);
console.log(mode === 2 ? 'HEDGING (multiple positions/symbol)' : mode === 0 ? 'NETTING' : 'EXCHANGE');

docs.title: 4) Pending-order budget
docs.text:
const limit = await account.accountInfoInteger(P.ACCOUNT_LIMIT_ORDERS);
console.log('max pending orders:', limit || 'unlimited');

docs.title: 5) FIFO rule check
docs.text:
const fifo = (await account.accountInfoInteger(P.ACCOUNT_FIFO_CLOSE)) === 1;
if (fifo) console.log('positions must be closed in FIFO order');

docs.title: 6) Read a batch concurrently
docs.text:
const P = AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType;
const [login, leverage, tradeMode, marginMode] = await Promise.all([
  account.accountInfoInteger(P.ACCOUNT_LOGIN),
  account.accountInfoInteger(P.ACCOUNT_LEVERAGE),
  account.accountInfoInteger(P.ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE),
  account.accountInfoInteger(P.ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE),
]);
console.log({ login, leverage, tradeMode, marginMode });

docs.title: Trading-enabled guard
docs.text:
async function tradingEnabled(account: MT5Account): Promise<boolean> {
  const P = AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType;
  const [acc, ea] = await Promise.all([
    account.accountInfoInteger(P.ACCOUNT_TRADE_ALLOWED),
    account.accountInfoInteger(P.ACCOUNT_TRADE_EXPERT),
  ]);
  return acc === 1 && ea === 1;
}

docs.title: Describe the account configuration
docs.text:
async function describeConfig(account: MT5Account): Promise<string> {
  const P = AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType;
  const [lev, mm] = await Promise.all([
    account.accountInfoInteger(P.ACCOUNT_LEVERAGE),
    account.accountInfoInteger(P.ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE),
  ]);
  const margin = mm === 2 ? 'hedging' : mm === 0 ? 'netting' : 'exchange';
  return `1:${lev}, ${margin}`;
}

docs.text:
• AccountSummary — login, leverage, modes and flags in one call.
  • AccountInfoDouble · AccountInfoString
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service.getAccountInteger.

docs.title: 🔤 Getting Account String Properties
docs.text:
Request: one text account property (AccountInfoStringData → a string) from MT5 — holder name, trade server, deposit currency, or broker name, selected by an enum.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account.accountInfoString(...) (from @metarpc/nodemt5)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.AccountInformation
  • Proto definition: AccountInfoString (in mt5-term-api-account-information.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.AccountInformation
  • Method: AccountInfoString(AccountInfoStringRequest) → AccountInfoStringReply
  • Low-level client (generated): AccountInformationClient.accountInfoString(request, metadata, opts)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC that returns a single text account property, chosen by an AccountInfoStringPropertyType value.
  • Why you need it. Read the deposit currency to format money, or the server / broker / holder name for a header.
  • Sanity check. ACCOUNT_CURRENCY returns a 3-letter code like "USD".

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use it for the account's textual identity:

  • Currency — to label and format every money figure.
  • Server — which trade server you're connected to (e.g. MetaQuotes-Demo).
  • Name / Company — for dashboards and reports.

docs.title: 📚 Tutorial
docs.text:
1. Connect so the SDK has a terminal session.
  2. Pick the property from AccountInfoStringPropertyType, e.g. ACCOUNT_CURRENCY.
  3. Call account.accountInfoString(propertyId) — it builds the request, sends it, and unwraps getRequestedValue().
  4. Use the string — e.g. append the currency to your balance readouts.
import { MT5Account, AccountInformationPb } from '@metarpc/nodemt5';
const P = AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoStringPropertyType;

const currency = await account.accountInfoString(P.ACCOUNT_CURRENCY);   // "USD"

docs.text:

class MT5Account {
  // Read one ACCOUNT_* string property. Pass an AccountInfoStringPropertyType value.
  // Returns getRequestedValue() directly.
  accountInfoString(propertyId: number, timeoutMs?: number): Promise<string>;
}

Request message:

AccountInfoStringRequest { AccountInfoStringPropertyType property_id = 1; }

Reply message:

AccountInfoStringReply {
  oneof response {
    AccountInfoStringData data = 1;   // getRequestedValue(): string
    Error error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description propertyId number (AccountInfoStringPropertyType) Which string property to read. timeoutMs number? Optional per-call deadline (default 15 s).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — AccountInfoStringData
docs.text: Field JS accessor Type Description requested value getRequestedValue() string The property's value. Returned directly.

docs.title: 🧱 Related enums (from proto)
docs.text: Access as AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoStringPropertyType.ACCOUNT_CURRENCY (a number).

docs.title: AccountInfoStringPropertyType
docs.text: Constant Meaning ACCOUNT_NAME Account holder's name. ACCOUNT_SERVER Trade server (e.g. MetaQuotes-Demo). ACCOUNT_CURRENCY Deposit currency (USD, EUR, …). ACCOUNT_COMPANY Broker / company name.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Currency drives formatting. Read ACCOUNT_CURRENCY once and reuse it to label balance, equity and P/L.
  • For everything at once, AccountSummary already returns name, server, company and currency.
  • Errors are exceptions — a failure rejects with an MrpcError.

docs.title: 1) Deposit currency
docs.text:
import { MT5Account, AccountInformationPb } from '@metarpc/nodemt5';
const P = AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoStringPropertyType;

const currency = await account.accountInfoString(P.ACCOUNT_CURRENCY);
console.log('currency:', currency);

docs.title: 2) Trade server
docs.text:
const server = await account.accountInfoString(P.ACCOUNT_SERVER);
console.log('connected to', server);

docs.title: 3) Account holder & broker
docs.text:
const [name, company] = await Promise.all([
  account.accountInfoString(P.ACCOUNT_NAME),
  account.accountInfoString(P.ACCOUNT_COMPANY),
]);
console.log(`${name} @ ${company}`);

docs.title: 4) Build a header line
docs.text:
const P = AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoStringPropertyType;
const [name, server, currency] = await Promise.all([
  account.accountInfoString(P.ACCOUNT_NAME),
  account.accountInfoString(P.ACCOUNT_SERVER),
  account.accountInfoString(P.ACCOUNT_CURRENCY),
]);
console.log(`${name} · ${server} · ${currency}`);

docs.title: 5) Format money with the right currency
docs.text:
const P = AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoStringPropertyType;
const D = AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoDoublePropertyType;
const [currency, balance] = await Promise.all([
  account.accountInfoString(P.ACCOUNT_CURRENCY),
  account.accountInfoDouble(D.ACCOUNT_BALANCE),
]);
console.log(`${balance.toFixed(2)} ${currency}`);

docs.title: 6) Verify you're on the expected server
docs.text:
const server = await account.accountInfoString(P.ACCOUNT_SERVER);
if (server !== 'MetaQuotes-Demo') console.warn('unexpected server:', server);

docs.title: Cache the currency once
docs.text:
let cachedCurrency: string | null = null;
async function currency(account: MT5Account): Promise<string> {
  if (cachedCurrency) return cachedCurrency;
  const P = AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoStringPropertyType;
  cachedCurrency = await account.accountInfoString(P.ACCOUNT_CURRENCY);
  return cachedCurrency;
}

docs.title: One-line account header
docs.text:
async function header(account: MT5Account): Promise<string> {
  const P = AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoStringPropertyType;
  const [name, server, currency] = await Promise.all([
    account.accountInfoString(P.ACCOUNT_NAME),
    account.accountInfoString(P.ACCOUNT_SERVER),
    account.accountInfoString(P.ACCOUNT_CURRENCY),
  ]);
  return `${name} · ${server} · ${currency}`;
}
