  • Low-level: Trading Operations — Overview.
  • High-level: MT5Sugar.buy / sell / closeAll — one-liners with risk-based sizing.

docs.title: 🎯 Summary
docs.text: Trading methods replace protobuf request-building with plain objects and string actions, and decode the result into a typed OrderResult / CloseResult / OrderCheckResult. The retcode rule stays: 10009 = DONE, and the calculators (calculateMargin / calculateProfit) let you size and validate before committing.

docs.title: MT5Service — Market Depth Methods (Mid-Level API)
docs.text:
Level-II order book as a plain BookInfo[] — subscribe, read, unsubscribe.

🧩 API Layer: MID-LEVEL — a facade over the low-level Market Depth (DOM) group.

Implementation: src/MT5Service.ts. Demos: examples/demos/service/04_service_demo.js.

← MT5Service Overview · low-level group ↓

docs.title: 🎯 Why these methods exist
docs.text:
On MT5Account, reading the book means a MarketBookGetRequest and unwrapping a repeated protobuf list. MT5Service returns a mapped array of plain objects and simplifies subscribe/release to a boolean:

// Mid-level
const ok   = await service.subscribeMarketDepth('EURUSD');
const book = await service.getMarketDepth('EURUSD'); // → BookInfo[]
await service.unsubscribeMarketDepth('EURUSD');

docs.title: 📋 All methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Purpose subscribeMarketDepth(symbol) Promise<boolean> Open the book on the gateway. getMarketDepth(symbol) Promise<BookInfo[]> Current book snapshot (rows). unsubscribeMarketDepth(symbol) Promise<boolean> Close the subscription.

Call subscribe → get (repeatedly) → unsubscribe.

docs.title: 📦 BookInfo (DTO)
docs.text:
Field Type Description type number MQL5 ENUM_BOOK_TYPE — 1 = sell, 2 = buy, 3/4 = sell/buy market. price number Level price. volume number Volume (integer units). volumeReal number Volume (real/lots).

⚠️ DOM availability. Depth of Market is usually not available for forex on demo accounts — subscribeMarketDepth may resolve false. It's meaningful for exchange-traded instruments.

docs.title: 1) Subscribe and read once
docs.text:
if (await service.subscribeMarketDepth('EURUSD')) {
  const book = await service.getMarketDepth('EURUSD');
  console.log(`${book.length} levels`);
  await service.unsubscribeMarketDepth('EURUSD');
} else {
  console.log('DOM not available for this symbol/account');
}

docs.title: 2) Split by side
docs.text:
const book = await service.getMarketDepth('EURUSD');
const buys  = book.filter((r) => r.type === 2);
const sells = book.filter((r) => r.type === 1);
console.log('best bid', Math.max(...buys.map((r) => r.price)), 'best ask', Math.min(...sells.map((r) => r.price)));

docs.title: 3) Order-book imbalance
docs.text:
const book = await service.getMarketDepth('EURUSD');
let buyVol = 0, sellVol = 0;
for (const r of book) (r.type === 2 ? (buyVol += r.volumeReal) : (sellVol += r.volumeReal));
console.log(buyVol > sellVol ? '📈 bullish pressure' : '📉 bearish pressure');

docs.title: 4) Poll with cleanup
docs.text:
await service.subscribeMarketDepth('EURUSD');
const timer = setInterval(async () => {
  const book = await service.getMarketDepth('EURUSD');
  console.log(`${new Date().toLocaleTimeString()} — ${book.length} levels`);
}, 1000);

// later:
clearInterval(timer);
await service.unsubscribeMarketDepth('EURUSD');

docs.title: 🔧 Notes & gotchas
docs.text:
• Subscribe first. getMarketDepth returns rows only after a successful subscribeMarketDepth.
  • Add to Market Watch. Use symbolSelect if the symbol isn't selected.
  • Always unsubscribe. Release the book when done to free the subscription.

docs.title: 📚 Related
docs.text:
• MT5Service Overview · Symbol Methods · Streaming Methods.
  • Low-level: Market Depth (DOM) — Overview.

docs.title: 🎯 Summary
docs.text: Market Depth methods wrap the DOM subscription into three calls that return booleans and a mapped BookInfo[], so you work with plain { type, price, volume, volumeReal } rows instead of protobuf lists.

docs.title: MT5Service — Streaming Methods (Mid-Level API)
docs.text:
Real-time subscriptions with a simple callback model — ticks as typed Quotes, plus trade, P&L, ticket and transaction streams.

🧩 API Layer: MID-LEVEL — a facade over the low-level Streaming Methods group.

Implementation: src/MT5Service.ts. Demos: examples/demos/service/05_service_streaming.js.

← MT5Service Overview · low-level group ↓

docs.title: 🎯 The subscription model
docs.text:
Every streaming method returns a Subscription — { unsubscribe(): void } — and calls your callback per payload. Errors go to the optional onError. The SDK attaches the session guid + api key automatically — just connect() first.

const sub = service.streamTicks(['EURUSD'], (quote) => { /* … */ });
// later:
sub.unsubscribe();

Always keep the Subscription and unsubscribe() when done — an un-cancelled stream keeps the gRPC call (and terminal) alive.

docs.title: 📋 All methods
docs.text:
Method Callback payload Notes streamTicks(symbols, cb, onError?) Quote (mapped) Live Bid/Ask for one or more symbols. streamTradeUpdates(cb, onError?) raw OnTradeData "Something changed" — orders/positions/deals. streamPositionProfits(cb, onError?) raw OnPositionProfitData Periodic open-position P&L. streamOpenedTickets(cb, onError?) raw OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsData Periodic ticket snapshots. streamTransactions(cb, onError?) raw OnTradeTransactionData Raw trade-transaction detail.

Mapped vs raw. streamTicks delivers a typed Quote ({ symbol, bid, ask, last, volume, time, flags }). The other four pass the raw low-level *Data message — read it with the same getXxx() accessors documented on the low-level streaming pages. This keeps every field reachable without a lossy mapping.

docs.title: 📖 Method details
docs.text:
// Ticks → typed Quote
const t = service.streamTicks(['EURUSD', 'GBPUSD'], (q) => {
  console.log(`${q.symbol}: ${q.bid}/${q.ask}`);
}, (e) => console.error(e.message));

// Trade events (raw payload)
const u = service.streamTradeUpdates((data) => console.log('event type', data.getType()));

// Periodic P&L (raw payload)
const p = service.streamPositionProfits((data) => {
  for (const pos of data.getUpdatedPositionsList()) {
    console.log(`#${pos.getTicket()} ${pos.getPositionSymbol()} ${pos.getProfit().toFixed(2)}`);
  }
});

// Ticket snapshots (raw payload)
const k = service.streamOpenedTickets((data) => {
  console.log('positions:', data.getPositionTicketsList());
});

// Transactions (raw payload)
const x = service.streamTransactions((data) => {
  const tx = data.getTradeTransaction();
  console.log('deal#', tx.getDealTicket(), 'order#', tx.getOrderTicket());
});

docs.title: 1) Live price print
docs.text: const sub = service.streamTicks(['EURUSD'], (q) => console.log(q.symbol, q.bid, q.ask));

docs.title: 2) Spread alert
docs.text:
const sub = service.streamTicks(['EURUSD'], (q) => {
  const spread = q.ask - q.bid;
  if (spread > 0.0003) console.warn(`wide spread: ${(spread * 1e5).toFixed(0)} pts`);
});

docs.title: 3) Re-pull the blotter on any trade event
docs.text:
const sub = service.streamTradeUpdates(async () => {
  const { positions } = await service.getOpenedOrders();
  console.log('positions now:', positions.length);
});

docs.title: 4) Floating-P&L ticker
docs.text:
const sub = service.streamPositionProfits((data) => {
  const total = data.getUpdatedPositionsList().reduce((s: number, p: any) => s + p.getProfit(), 0);
  console.log('floating:', total.toFixed(2));
});

docs.title: 5) Stop when flat
docs.text:
const sub = service.streamOpenedTickets((data) => {
  if (data.getPositionTicketsList().length === 0) { console.log('all closed'); sub.unsubscribe(); }
});

docs.title: 6) Several streams, one cleanup
docs.text:
const subs = [
  service.streamTicks(['EURUSD'], (q) => console.log('[TICK]', q.bid)),
  service.streamTradeUpdates((d) => console.log('[TRADE]', d.getType())),
];
// later:
for (const s of subs) s.unsubscribe();

docs.title: 🔧 Notes & gotchas
docs.text:
• Callbacks, not channels — no manual loop; the SDK reads the stream for you.
  • streamTicks is high-frequency — keep the callback cheap.
  • P&L has no symbol filter — streamPositionProfits streams all positions; filter by getPositionSymbol() in the callback.
  • Always unsubscribe() — streams don't stop on their own.
  • Need typed objects for every stream? Drop to the low-level pages, or use MT5Sugar.onTick / onTrade.

docs.title: 📚 Related
docs.text:
• MT5Service Overview · Positions & Orders Methods · Trading Methods.
  • Low-level: Streaming Methods — Overview.
  • High-level: MT5Sugar — onTick / onTrade one-liners.

docs.title: 🎯 Summary
docs.text: Streaming methods expose a uniform Subscription callback model. streamTicks gives you typed Quotes; the trade/P&L/ticket/transaction streams pass the raw low-level payload so no field is lost. Keep the handle, unsubscribe() when done.

docs.title: MT5Service — Mid-Level API Overview
docs.text:
A convenient wrapper over MT5Account that returns clean TypeScript objects instead of protobuf messages.

🧩 API Layer: MID-LEVEL — the balance between low-level (MT5Account) and high-level (MT5Sugar).

docs.title: ⚠️ Same calls, cleaner results
docs.text:
MT5Service and MT5Account make the same gRPC calls — the difference is the return type, not the logic.

// Low-level (MT5Account) — you unwrap the protobuf:
import { MT5Account, AccountInformationPb } from '@metarpc/nodemt5';
const d = await account.accountInfoDouble(
  AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoDoublePropertyType.ACCOUNT_BALANCE,
);
const balance = d.getRequestedValue();     // ← unwrap

// Mid-level (MT5Service) — you get the value:
const balance = await service.getAccountDouble(
  AccountInformationPb.AccountInfoDoublePropertyType.ACCOUNT_BALANCE,
);                                          // ← direct number

What the mid layer does for you

  • ✅ Builds the protobuf *Request from plain arguments.
  • ✅ Unwraps the *Data reply (getRequestedValue(), getTotal(), lists…).
  • ✅ Converts protobuf Timestamp → JS epoch (number, ms where noted).
  • ✅ Returns typed objects (AccountInfo, Quote, Position, …), not protobuf.
  • ✅ Decodes enums to friendly strings (tradeMode: 'DEMO' | 'REAL', action: 'BUY').

Both layers are equally valid — pick the altitude you prefer. For one-liners, go up again to MT5Sugar.

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture layers
docs.text:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  MT5Sugar      one-liners, risk-based sizing│  ← highest
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  MT5Service    plain args → typed objects   │  ← YOU ARE HERE
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  MT5Account    raw protobuf / gRPC          │  ← lowest
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Each layer owns the one below it: MT5Sugar owns an MT5Service, which owns an MT5Account. From here you can always drop down with service.account().

docs.title: 🧱 Construction & lifecycle
docs.text:
import { MT5Service } from '@metarpc/nodemt5';

// create() builds the MT5Account underneath for you
const service = MT5Service.create('mt5.mrpc.pro', 443);
await service.connect(login, 'password', 'MetaQuotes-Demo');

const acc = await service.getAccountSummary();   // AccountInfo
console.log(acc.balance, acc.currency, acc.server);

await service.disconnect();
  • MT5Service.create(host?, port?, apiKey?, id?) → a service wrapping a fresh MT5Account (defaults mt5.mrpc.pro:443).
  • service.account() → the underlying MT5Account (drop down a layer any time).
  • service.connect(login, password, server) — accepts a { user, password, server } options object too.
  • service.disconnect(deleteOnDisconnect?) — pass true to free the terminal (otherwise it stays warm).

Tuning timeouts. Unary reads use the underlying account.callTimeoutMs (default 30000); set service.account().callTimeoutMs = 60000 to change it.

docs.title: 📁 Method groups (40+ methods)
docs.text: # Group Methods 1 Account Methods (4) getAccountSummary · getAccountDouble · getAccountInteger · getAccountString 2 Symbol Methods (17) getSymbolsTotal · symbolExist · getSymbolName · symbolSelect · isSymbolSynchronized · ensureSymbol · getSymbolTick · getSymbolDouble/Integer/String · getSymbolParams · getSymbolParamsMany · getSymbolMarginRate · getSymbolSessionQuote/Trade · priceHistory 3 Position & Order Methods (6) getPositionsTotal · getOpenedOrders · getOpenedTickets · getPositions · getOrderHistory · getPositionsHistory 4 Trading Methods (6) placeOrder · modifyOrder · closeOrder · checkOrder · calculateMargin · calculateProfit 5 Market Depth Methods (3) subscribeMarketDepth · getMarketDepth · unsubscribeMarketDepth 6 Streaming Methods (5) streamTicks · streamTradeUpdates · streamPositionProfits · streamOpenedTickets · streamTransactions

docs.title: 🧾 The typed objects (DTOs)
docs.text:
All plain TS interfaces (each group page documents the full shape):

DTO From Key fields AccountInfo getAccountSummary login, balance, equity, freeMargin, marginLevel, leverage, currency, tradeMode, serverTime Quote getSymbolTick, tick stream symbol, bid, ask, last, volume, time (ms) SymbolParams getSymbolParams(Many) ~30 fields: digits, point, spread, contractSize, volumeMin/Max/Step, … Bar priceHistory time, open, high, low, close, tickVolume, realVolume Position / PendingOrder getOpenedOrders / getPositions ticket, symbol, type, volume, priceOpen, profit, magic, … HistoryOrder / HistoryDeal / HistoryPosition history methods closed orders, deals, positions with P&L OrderRequest → OrderResult placeOrder request: symbol, action, volume, stopLoss?, …; result: ticket, retcode, deal, price CloseRequest → CloseResult closeOrder ticket, volume? → retcode, closeMode OrderCheckResult checkOrder returnedCode (0 = ok), margin, marginFree, marginLevel, comment SymbolMarginRate · SessionTime · BookInfo margin/session/DOM initial/maintenanceMarginRate · from/to · type, price, volume, volumeReal

docs.title: 1) Account snapshot
docs.text:
const a = await service.getAccountSummary();
console.log(`${a.name} #${a.login} · ${a.balance} ${a.currency} · 1:${a.leverage}`);

docs.title: 2) Current price
docs.text:
const t = await service.getSymbolTick('EURUSD');
console.log(`Bid ${t.bid}, Ask ${t.ask}, Spread ${(t.ask - t.bid).toFixed(5)}`);

docs.title: 3) Validate → place an order
docs.text:
const chk = await service.checkOrder({ symbol: 'EURUSD', action: 'BUY', volume: 0.1 });
if (chk.returnedCode !== 0) throw new Error(chk.comment);

const r = await service.placeOrder({ symbol: 'EURUSD', action: 'BUY', volume: 0.1, stopLoss: 1.08, takeProfit: 1.09 });
console.log(r.retcode === 10009 ? `✅ ticket #${r.ticket}` : `❌ ${r.retcodeDescription}`);

docs.title: 4) Live price + floating P&L
docs.text:
const t = service.streamTicks(['EURUSD'], (q) => console.log('tick', q.bid, q.ask));
const p = service.streamPositionProfits((data) => {
  const total = data.getUpdatedPositionsList().reduce((s: number, x: any) => s + x.getProfit(), 0);
  console.log('floating:', total.toFixed(2));
});
// later: t.unsubscribe(); p.unsubscribe();

docs.title: 📊 Low-level vs mid-level
docs.text: Aspect MT5Account (low) MT5Service (mid) Arguments build a *Request, set fields plain args / objects Return protobuf *Data, call getXxx() typed JS object Enums ...Pb.Enum.CONSTANT friendly strings ('BUY', 'DEMO') Timestamps getSeconds() / raw JS epoch number Best for every field, full control everyday app code

docs.title: 💡 When to use which
docs.text:
Use MT5Service (recommended) for application code — dashboards, bots, reports — where typed objects read cleaner and you don't need protobuf internals.

Drop to MT5Account when you need a field the DTO doesn't expose, or full control over the exact request. You can always reach it via service.account().

Go up to MT5Sugar when you want one-liners (buy, sell, price, closeAll) with smart defaults and risk-based sizing.

docs.title: 🔧 Best practices
docs.text:
1. Handle errors with try/catch. Every method rejects on failure — a server rejection throws MrpcError (carrying mqlCode / tradeCode), a transport failure throws the gRPC error.
try {
  const a = await service.getAccountSummary();
} catch (e) {
  console.error('failed:', (e as Error).message);
}

  1. Check the trade retcode. placeOrder / modifyOrder / closeOrder reject only on transport errors — a broker rejection comes back in the result. 10009 = DONE; checkOrder.returnedCode === 0 = would be accepted.

  2. Tune the timeout via service.account().callTimeoutMs for slow links or heavy history pulls.

  3. Always unsubscribe() streaming handles when done — they don't stop on their own.

  4. Free the terminal with service.disconnect(true) at the end of a one-shot run (a trial allows one terminal per IP).

docs.title: 🎯 Summary
docs.text: MT5Service is the everyday layer: the same gRPC calls as MT5Account, but plain arguments in and typed objects out — no manual requests, no .getXxx() chains, enums decoded to friendly strings, timestamps as JS epochs. Drop to MT5Account for full control, go up to MT5Sugar for one-liners.

docs.title: MT5Sugar — Connection (High-Level API)
docs.text:
One-liner connect and liveness checks — the fastest way onto the terminal.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — one-liners with smart defaults over MT5Service / MT5Account.

Implementation: src/MT5Sugar.ts. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/06_sugar_basics.js.

← MT5Sugar API Overview

docs.title: 🧱 Build the stack & reach the layers below
docs.text:
import { MT5Sugar } from '@metarpc/nodemt5';

// create() builds Service → Account underneath in one call
const sugar = MT5Sugar.create('mt5.mrpc.pro', 443);

await sugar.quickConnect(5057947437, 'password', 'MetaQuotes-Demo');
// … use it …
await sugar.service().disconnect(true);
  • MT5Sugar.create(host?, port?, apiKey?, id?) → the whole stack (defaults mt5.mrpc.pro:443).
  • sugar.service() → the MT5Service underneath · sugar.account() → the MT5Account.

docs.title: 📋 Methods
docs.text: Method Returns Purpose quickConnect(login?, password?, server?) Promise<boolean> Connect; falls back to env vars. isConnected() boolean true after a successful connect. ping() Promise<boolean> Liveness probe — terminal connected & alive.

docs.title: quickConnect(login?, password?, server?)
docs.text:
Connects by login / password / server. Any omitted argument falls back to an env var — MT5_LOGIN, MT5_PASSWORD, MT5_SERVER — so you can keep credentials out of code. Throws MrpcError if none of the three is available.

// explicit
await sugar.quickConnect(5057947437, 'password', 'MetaQuotes-Demo');

// from env (MT5_LOGIN / MT5_PASSWORD / MT5_SERVER)
await sugar.quickConnect();

docs.title: isConnected()
docs.text: Synchronous flag — no round-trip. true once quickConnect has succeeded.

docs.title: ping()
docs.text: A lightweight health check against the terminal; returns false instead of throwing if the terminal is down — safe to call in a loop.

docs.title: 1) Connect from environment
docs.text:
const sugar = MT5Sugar.create();
if (!(await sugar.quickConnect())) throw new Error('connect failed');
console.log('connected:', sugar.isConnected());

docs.title: 2) Reconnect guard before an action
docs.text:
if (!sugar.isConnected() || !(await sugar.ping())) {
  await sugar.quickConnect();
}

docs.title: 3) Liveness heartbeat
docs.text:
const timer = setInterval(async () => {
  console.log(new Date().toLocaleTimeString(), (await sugar.ping()) ? '🟢 alive' : '🔴 down');
}, 5000);
// later: clearInterval(timer);

docs.title: 4) Clean shutdown (frees the trial terminal)
docs.text:
try {
  // … work …
} finally {
  await sugar.service().disconnect(true); // true = delete the terminal, free the slot
}

docs.title: 🔧 Notes
docs.text:
• Env fallback makes quickConnect() with no args the norm in scripts — set MT5_LOGIN / MT5_PASSWORD / MT5_SERVER.
  • ping() never throws — it's a boolean probe, unlike other calls which reject on error.
  • Free the terminal with disconnect(true) at the end of a one-shot run (a trial allows one terminal per IP).

docs.title: 📚 Related
docs.text:
• MT5Sugar API Overview · Balance & Margin · Prices & Quotes.
  • Down: MT5Service.connect / disconnect.

docs.title: 🎯 Summary
docs.text: Connection sugar is three calls: quickConnect (explicit or from env), isConnected (sync flag) and ping (safe liveness probe). create() builds the whole stack; service() / account() drop you to the layers below.

docs.title: MT5Sugar — Risk Management (High-Level API)
docs.text:
Size positions by risk, cap by free margin, pre-flight a trade, and compute SL/TP levels.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — composed calculators over MT5Service.

Implementation: src/MT5Sugar.ts. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/10_sugar_advanced.js.

← MT5Sugar API Overview

docs.title: 📋 Methods
docs.text: Method Returns Purpose calculatePositionSize(symbol, riskPercent, stopLossPips) Promise<number> Lots so a stopLossPips stop risks riskPercent% of balance. getMaxLotSize(symbol) Promise<number> Largest lot 80% of free margin can open. canOpenPosition(symbol, volume) Promise<{ ok: boolean; reason: string }> Pre-flight: availability, volume bounds, margin. calculateRequiredMargin(symbol, volume) Promise<number> Margin for volume lots at the current ask. calculateSLTP(symbol, direction, entryPrice, stopLossPips, takeProfitPips) Promise<{ sl: number; tp: number }> Absolute SL/TP from pip distances.

docs.title: calculatePositionSize(symbol, riskPercent, stopLossPips)
docs.text: Returns a lot size such that hitting a stopLossPips stop loses about riskPercent% of the current balance. Uses the symbol's tick value / tick size and clamps to the symbol's min/max/step. Throws if stopLossPips <= 0 or tick data is bad.

docs.title: getMaxLotSize(symbol)
docs.text: Largest lot the current free margin can open, using only 80% of it as a safety buffer. Falls back to volumeMin if margin-per-lot can't be computed.

docs.title: canOpenPosition(symbol, volume)
docs.text: A single pre-flight check returning { ok, reason }. Fails (ok: false, with a human reason) when the symbol is unavailable, the volume is below min / above max, or the required margin exceeds free margin.

docs.title: calculateRequiredMargin(symbol, volume)
docs.text: Margin to open volume lots at the current ask (wraps MT5Service.calculateMargin('BUY', …)).

docs.title: calculateSLTP(symbol, direction, entryPrice, stopLossPips, takeProfitPips)
docs.text: Absolute sl / tp prices from pip distances. direction is 'BUY' or 'SELL'; pass entryPrice = 0 to use the live ask (BUY) / bid (SELL). Geometry: BUY → sl below, tp above; SELL → mirrored.

docs.title: 1) Risk-based sizing
docs.text: const lots = await sugar.calculatePositionSize('EURUSD', 1, 20); // risk 1% over a 20-pip stop

docs.title: 2) Cap by free margin
docs.text:
const max = await sugar.getMaxLotSize('EURUSD');
console.log('max lots:', max);

docs.title: 3) Pre-flight before sending
docs.text:
const { ok, reason } = await sugar.canOpenPosition('EURUSD', 0.5);
if (!ok) throw new Error(reason);
await sugar.buyMarket('EURUSD', 0.5);

docs.title: 4) Margin for a size
docs.text: console.log('margin for 1 lot:', (await sugar.calculateRequiredMargin('EURUSD', 1)).toFixed(2));

docs.title: 5) SL/TP from pips at market
docs.text:
const { sl, tp } = await sugar.calculateSLTP('EURUSD', 'BUY', 0, 20, 40); // live ask, 20/40 pips
await sugar.buyMarketWithSLTP('EURUSD', 0.1, sl, tp);

docs.title: 6) Full risk-managed entry
docs.text:
const symbol = 'EURUSD';
const lots = await sugar.calculatePositionSize(symbol, 1, 20);
const { ok, reason } = await sugar.canOpenPosition(symbol, lots);
if (!ok) throw new Error(reason);
const { sl, tp } = await sugar.calculateSLTP(symbol, 'BUY', 0, 20, 40);
await sugar.buyMarketWithSLTP(symbol, lots, sl, tp);

docs.title: 🔧 Notes
docs.text:
• Pips, not points. Sizing/levels use pips (point × 10 on 3/5-digit symbols) — consistent with the trading helpers.
  • getMaxLotSize keeps a 20% buffer (uses 80% of free margin).
  • calculatePositionSize risks the balance, clamped to the symbol's volume rules.
  • calculateRequiredMargin prices at the ask (BUY side) — a good proxy for either direction.

docs.title: 📚 Related
docs.text:
• Trading Helpers — pip-distance entries · Trading with SL/TP · Symbol Information.
  • Down: MT5Service.calculateMargin.

docs.title: 🎯 Summary
docs.text: Risk sugar turns account and symbol facts into decisions: size by risk (calculatePositionSize), cap by margin (getMaxLotSize), pre-flight (canOpenPosition), margin cost (calculateRequiredMargin) and SL/TP levels (calculateSLTP). Compose them for a fully risk-managed entry.

docs.title: MT5Sugar — Trading Helpers (High-Level API)
docs.text:
Market orders with SL/TP given as pip distances from entry — the most convenient way to open a protected trade.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — composed over calculateSLTP + Trading with SL/TP.

Implementation: src/MT5Sugar.ts. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/07_sugar_trading.js.

← MT5Sugar API Overview

docs.title: 📋 Methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Order buyMarketWithPips(symbol, volume, stopLossPips, takeProfitPips) Promise<number> Market BUY; SL/TP as pip distances. sellMarketWithPips(symbol, volume, stopLossPips, takeProfitPips) Promise<number> Market SELL; SL/TP as pip distances.

These compute absolute levels from the current price via calculateSLTP, then place the order through the SL/TP variants. They return the ticket and throw MrpcError on rejection, like the rest of the trading sugar.

Looking for calculateSLTP itself? It lives in Risk Management.

docs.title: 1) BUY with 20/40 pips
docs.text: const ticket = await sugar.buyMarketWithPips('EURUSD', 0.1, 20, 40); // 20-pip SL, 40-pip TP

docs.title: 2) SELL with symmetric stops
docs.text: await sugar.sellMarketWithPips('EURUSD', 0.1, 30, 30);

docs.title: 3) Risk-sized, pip-defined entry
docs.text:
const lots = await sugar.calculatePositionSize('EURUSD', 1, 20); // 1% risk, 20-pip stop
const ticket = await sugar.buyMarketWithPips('EURUSD', lots, 20, 40);

docs.title: 4) Guarded entry
docs.text:
const { ok, reason } = await sugar.canOpenPosition('EURUSD', 0.1);
if (!ok) throw new Error(reason);
await sugar.buyMarketWithPips('EURUSD', 0.1, 25, 50);

docs.title: 5) Handle a closed market
docs.text:
try {
  await sugar.sellMarketWithPips('EURUSD', 0.1, 20, 40);
} catch (e) {
  if ((e as Error).message.includes('10018')) console.log('market closed');
  else throw e;
}

docs.title: 🔧 Notes
docs.text:
• Pip = point × 10 on 3/5-digit symbols, else point — the same convention as Risk Management.
  • Levels from the live quote. Entry defaults to the current ask (BUY) / bid (SELL).
  • Mind the stop level. SL/TP must clear getMinStopLevel or expect retcode 10016.

docs.title: 📚 Related
docs.text: • Risk Management — calculateSLTP, sizing · Trading with SL/TP — absolute-price variants · Simple Trading.

docs.title: 🎯 Summary
docs.text: Two helpers open a protected market trade from pip distances — the sugar you reach for when you think in pips. They pair naturally with calculatePositionSize for a fully sized, protected entry in a couple of lines.

docs.title: MT5Sugar — Account Information (High-Level API)
docs.text:
The full account snapshot, and a one-call win/loss summary of today.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — one-liners over MT5Service.

Implementation: src/MT5Sugar.ts. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/06_sugar_basics.js · 09_sugar_history.js.

← MT5Sugar API Overview

docs.title: 📋 Methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Value getAccountInfo() Promise<AccountInfo> Full account snapshot. getDailyStats() Promise<DailyStats> Today's win/loss summary.

AccountInfo (login, balance, equity, freeMargin, leverage, currency, tradeMode, …) is documented in MT5Service → Account Methods.

docs.title: 📦 DailyStats (DTO)
docs.text:
Computed from the positions opened today (net = profit + swap + commission + fee):

Field Type Description totalDeals number Count of closed positions today. winningDeals number Of those, net ≥ 0. losingDeals number Of those, net < 0. winRate number winning / total, percent. totalProfit number Sum of net results. bestDeal number Largest single net. worstDeal number Smallest (most negative) net.

docs.title: 1) Account header
docs.text:
const a = await sugar.getAccountInfo();
console.log(`#${a.login} · ${a.balance} ${a.currency} · 1:${a.leverage} · ${a.tradeMode}`);

docs.title: 2) Today's scorecard
docs.text:
const s = await sugar.getDailyStats();
console.log(`${s.totalDeals} trades · win ${s.winRate.toFixed(0)}% · P&L ${s.totalProfit.toFixed(2)}`);
console.log(`best ${s.bestDeal.toFixed(2)} · worst ${s.worstDeal.toFixed(2)}`);

docs.title: 3) Demo vs real guard
docs.text: if ((await sugar.getAccountInfo()).tradeMode === 'REAL') console.log('🚨 live account');

docs.title: 4) Stop trading after a daily loss limit
docs.text:
const s = await sugar.getDailyStats();
if (s.totalProfit <= -100) {
  console.log('daily loss limit hit — flattening');
  await sugar.closeAllPositions();
}

docs.title: 5) Win-rate gate
docs.text:
const s = await sugar.getDailyStats();
if (s.totalDeals >= 10 && s.winRate < 40) console.log('⚠️ win rate low today');

docs.title: 🔧 Notes
docs.text:
• getDailyStats counts closed positions opened today (local day) — net includes swap, commission and fee, not just profit.
  • For other windows (week/month, custom range) use History & Statistics.
  • For single figures (balance, equity, free margin) use Balance & Margin.

docs.title: 📚 Related
docs.text:
• Balance & Margin · History & Statistics · Position Information.
  • Down: MT5Service.getAccountSummary.

docs.title: 🎯 Summary
docs.text: Two reads: getAccountInfo for the full snapshot, getDailyStats for a ready-made win/loss/P&L summary of today. Combine the latter with closeAllPositions to enforce a daily loss limit.

docs.title: MT5Sugar — Balance & Margin (High-Level API)
docs.text:
Single-number account reads — balance, equity, margin, free margin, level, floating profit.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — one-liners over MT5Service.

Implementation: src/MT5Sugar.ts. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/06_sugar_basics.js.

← MT5Sugar API Overview

docs.title: 📋 Methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Value getBalance() Promise<number> Balance (excludes floating P/L). getEquity() Promise<number> Equity (balance + floating P/L). getMargin() Promise<number> Margin currently in use. getFreeMargin() Promise<number> Free margin for new positions. getMarginLevel() Promise<number> Margin level, % (0 when flat). getProfit() Promise<number> Floating profit (equity − balance).

Each reads a field of the account snapshot (getAccountSummary). When you need several figures at once, read the snapshot directly — one round-trip instead of many.

docs.title: 1) Quick balance line
docs.text: console.log(`Balance ${await sugar.getBalance()} · Equity ${await sugar.getEquity()}`);

docs.title: 2) Margin-level health
docs.text:
const level = await sugar.getMarginLevel();
if (level > 0 && level < 100)      console.warn('⚠️ margin level critical');
else if (level > 0 && level < 200) console.warn('⚠️ low margin level');

docs.title: 3) Floating P&L watch
docs.text:
const timer = setInterval(async () => {
  console.log('floating:', (await sugar.getProfit()).toFixed(2));
}, 2000);
// later: clearInterval(timer);

docs.title: 4) Prefer one snapshot for several values
docs.text:
// ❌ three round-trips
const b = await sugar.getBalance(), e = await sugar.getEquity(), f = await sugar.getFreeMargin();

// ✅ one round-trip
const a = await sugar.service().getAccountSummary();
console.log(a.balance, a.equity, a.freeMargin);

docs.title: 5) Affordability gate
docs.text:
const free = await sugar.getFreeMargin();
if (free < 50) console.log('too little free margin to trade');

docs.title: 🔧 Notes
docs.text:
• getProfit() is floating P&L, computed as equity − balance — not realized profit (see History & Statistics for that).
  • getMarginLevel() is 0 when flat (no open positions → no used margin).
  • Batching: for 2+ values, call sugar.service().getAccountSummary() once rather than several getters.

docs.title: 📚 Related
docs.text:
• Account Information — full snapshot & daily stats · Risk Management — sizing from free margin.
  • Down: MT5Service.getAccountSummary.

docs.title: 🎯 Summary
docs.text: Six one-liners return single account figures straight as numbers. They're convenient for a single value or a quick check; for a dashboard of several figures, read getAccountSummary() once.

docs.title: MT5Sugar — Prices & Quotes (High-Level API)
docs.text:
Bid, ask, spread and a compact price snapshot — plus a price-watch helper.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — one-liners over MT5Service.

Implementation: src/MT5Sugar.ts. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/06_sugar_basics.js.

← MT5Sugar API Overview

docs.title: 📋 Methods
docs.text: Method Returns Value getBid(symbol) Promise<number> Current bid. getAsk(symbol) Promise<number> Current ask. getSpread(symbol) Promise<number> ask − bid, in price units. getPriceInfo(symbol) Promise<PriceInfo> Bid / ask / spread-in-pips / time in one snapshot. waitForPrice(symbol, targetBid, timeoutMs?) Promise<PriceInfo \| null> Poll until the bid reaches a target.

docs.title: 📦 PriceInfo (DTO)
docs.text: Field Type Description symbol string Instrument. bid / ask number Best prices. spreadPips number Spread expressed in pips (pip = point × 10 on 3/5-digit symbols). time number Tick time — milliseconds since epoch.

docs.title: getBid / getAsk / getSpread
docs.text: Single values pulled from the live tick. getSpread returns the raw price difference; for the pip-normalised spread use getPriceInfo().spreadPips.

docs.title: getPriceInfo(symbol)
docs.text: One snapshot combining the tick and the symbol's pip size — bid, ask, spreadPips, time. Internally fetches the tick and the spec in parallel (Promise.all).

docs.title: waitForPrice(symbol, targetBid, timeoutMs = 10000)
docs.text: Polls (~every 500 ms) until the bid ≥ targetBid, then returns the PriceInfo seen. Pass targetBid = 0 to just wait for the next price. Returns null on timeout.

docs.title: 1) Spread right now
docs.text:
const info = await sugar.getPriceInfo('EURUSD');
console.log(`${info.symbol}: ${info.bid}/${info.ask} · ${info.spreadPips.toFixed(1)} pips`);

docs.title: 2) BUY only on a tight spread
docs.text:
if ((await sugar.getPriceInfo('EURUSD')).spreadPips <= 1.5) {
  await sugar.buyMarket('EURUSD', 0.1);
}

docs.title: 3) Wait for a breakout level
docs.text:
const hit = await sugar.waitForPrice('EURUSD', 1.1000, 30000);
console.log(hit ? `reached ${hit.bid}` : 'timed out');

docs.title: 4) Raw bid/ask
docs.text:
const [bid, ask] = [await sugar.getBid('EURUSD'), await sugar.getAsk('EURUSD')];
console.log('mid:', ((bid + ask) / 2).toFixed(5));

docs.title: 5) Entry price for a calc
docs.text:
const ask = await sugar.getAsk('XAUUSD');
const { sl, tp } = await sugar.calculateSLTP('XAUUSD', 'BUY', ask, 100, 200);

docs.title: 🔧 Notes
docs.text:
• Live source. These read the current tick — reliable, unlike stale property prices.
  • Pips vs price units. getSpread is in price units; PriceInfo.spreadPips is pip-normalised.
  • waitForPrice polls, not streams. For a continuous feed use streamTicks / onTick.

docs.title: 📚 Related
docs.text:
• Simple Trading · Trading Helpers — act on the price · Symbol Information — digits & stop level.
  • Down: MT5Service.getSymbolTick.

docs.title: 🎯 Summary
docs.text: Price sugar gives single values (getBid / getAsk / getSpread), a combined PriceInfo snapshot with pip-normalised spread, and waitForPrice to block until a level is reached. For continuous updates, drop to the tick stream.

docs.title: MT5Sugar — Simple Trading (High-Level API)
docs.text:
Place market and pending orders in one line — returns the ticket, throws on rejection.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — one-liners over MT5Service.placeOrder.

Implementation: src/MT5Sugar.ts. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/07_sugar_trading.js.

← MT5Sugar API Overview

docs.title: 🛑 Result model — ticket or throw
docs.text:
Unlike the lower layers (which hand back a result with a retcode), the trading sugar throws MrpcError on a broker rejection (retcode ≠ 10009) and otherwise returns the ticket number. So you wrap calls in try/catch instead of checking a code.

try {
  const ticket = await sugar.buyMarket('EURUSD', 0.1);
  console.log('opened #', ticket);
} catch (e) {
  console.error('rejected:', (e as Error).message); // carries the retcode
}

docs.title: 📋 Methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Order buyMarket(symbol, volume) Promise<number> Market BUY. sellMarket(symbol, volume) Promise<number> Market SELL. buyLimit(symbol, volume, price) Promise<number> BUY LIMIT at price. sellLimit(symbol, volume, price) Promise<number> SELL LIMIT at price. buyStop(symbol, volume, price) Promise<number> BUY STOP at price. sellStop(symbol, volume, price) Promise<number> SELL STOP at price.

Returns the ticket (the position ticket for a filled market order). Need SL/TP in the same call? → Trading with SL/TP or Trading Helpers.

docs.title: 1) Market BUY
docs.text:
const ticket = await sugar.buyMarket('EURUSD', 0.1);
console.log('position #', ticket);

docs.title: 2) Pending BUY LIMIT below market
docs.text:
const bid = await sugar.getBid('EURUSD');
const ticket = await sugar.buyLimit('EURUSD', 0.1, bid - 0.0020); // 20 pips below

docs.title: 3) Breakout SELL STOP
docs.text:
const bid = await sugar.getBid('EURUSD');
await sugar.sellStop('EURUSD', 0.1, bid - 0.0015);

docs.title: 4) Guard with canOpenPosition first
docs.text:
const { ok, reason } = await sugar.canOpenPosition('EURUSD', 0.1);
if (!ok) throw new Error(reason);
const ticket = await sugar.buyMarket('EURUSD', 0.1);

docs.title: 5) Handle a closed market gracefully
docs.text:
try {
  await sugar.buyMarket('EURUSD', 0.1);
} catch (e) {
  const msg = (e as Error).message;
  if (msg.includes('10018')) console.log('market closed — try later');
  else throw e;
}

docs.title: 🔧 Notes
docs.text:
• Throws, doesn't return a code. A rejection becomes an MrpcError whose message/code carries the retcode (e.g. 10018 market closed, 10019 no money, 10016 invalid stops).
  • Market vs pending. Market orders (buyMarket/sellMarket) fill at the live quote; *Limit / *Stop rest at price until triggered.
  • Volume rules. Respect the symbol's min/step — see canOpenPosition / getSymbolInfo.

docs.title: 📚 Related
docs.text:
• Trading with SL/TP · Trading Helpers — SL/TP in one call · Position Management — close/modify.
  • Down: MT5Service.placeOrder.

docs.title: 🎯 Summary
docs.text: Six one-liners place market or pending orders and return the ticket, throwing MrpcError on rejection. Pair them with canOpenPosition for a pre-flight check, or step up to the SL/TP variants when you need protective levels.

docs.title: MT5Sugar — Trading with SL/TP (High-Level API)
docs.text:
Place an order with absolute stop-loss and take-profit prices in a single call.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — one-liners over MT5Service.placeOrder.

Implementation: src/MT5Sugar.ts. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/07_sugar_trading.js.

← MT5Sugar API Overview

docs.title: 📋 Methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Order buyMarketWithSLTP(symbol, volume, sl, tp) Promise<number> Market BUY + SL/TP. sellMarketWithSLTP(symbol, volume, sl, tp) Promise<number> Market SELL + SL/TP. buyLimitWithSLTP(symbol, volume, price, sl, tp) Promise<number> BUY LIMIT at price + SL/TP. sellLimitWithSLTP(symbol, volume, price, sl, tp) Promise<number> SELL LIMIT at price + SL/TP.

sl / tp are absolute prices, not distances. For pip distances use buyMarketWithPips / sellMarketWithPips, or compute levels with calculateSLTP. Like Simple Trading, these return the ticket and throw MrpcError on rejection.

docs.title: 1) Market BUY with fixed levels
docs.text: const ticket = await sugar.buyMarketWithSLTP('EURUSD', 0.1, 1.0800, 1.0900);

docs.title: 2) Levels from pip distances via calculateSLTP
docs.text:
const ask = await sugar.getAsk('EURUSD');
const { sl, tp } = await sugar.calculateSLTP('EURUSD', 'BUY', ask, 20, 40); // 20 pip SL, 40 pip TP
const ticket = await sugar.buyMarketWithSLTP('EURUSD', 0.1, sl, tp);

docs.title: 3) Pending SELL LIMIT with protection
docs.text:
const bid = await sugar.getBid('EURUSD');
await sugar.sellLimitWithSLTP('EURUSD', 0.1, bid + 0.0020, bid + 0.0040, bid - 0.0020);

docs.title: 4) Risk-sized entry with SL/TP
docs.text:
const lots = await sugar.calculatePositionSize('EURUSD', 1, 20); // risk 1% over a 20-pip stop
const ask = await sugar.getAsk('EURUSD');
const { sl, tp } = await sugar.calculateSLTP('EURUSD', 'BUY', ask, 20, 40);
await sugar.buyMarketWithSLTP('EURUSD', lots, sl, tp);

docs.title: 5) Validate stops distance first
docs.text:
const minPts = await sugar.getMinStopLevel('EURUSD'); // minimum SL/TP distance, points
// ensure your sl/tp are at least minPts away from price, else expect retcode 10016

docs.title: 🔧 Notes
docs.text:
• Absolute prices. sl/tp are levels, not offsets — mind the symbol's digits.
  • Stops level. SL/TP closer than getMinStopLevel → rejection (10016).
  • BUY vs SELL geometry. For a BUY, sl < price < tp; for a SELL, tp < price < sl.

docs.title: 📚 Related
docs.text:
• Trading Helpers — pip-distance variants · Risk Management — calculateSLTP, sizing · Simple Trading.
  • Down: MT5Service.placeOrder.

docs.title: 🎯 Summary
docs.text: Four one-liners place market or limit orders with absolute SL/TP and return the ticket. Feed them levels from calculateSLTP, or use the pip-distance helpers when you think in pips rather than prices.

docs.title: MT5Sugar — Position Management (High-Level API)
docs.text:
Close and modify positions in one line — full, partial, all, by symbol, SL/TP.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — one-liners over MT5Service.closeOrder / modifyOrder.

Implementation: src/MT5Sugar.ts. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/08_sugar_positions.js.

← MT5Sugar API Overview

docs.title: 📋 Methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Action closePosition(ticket) Promise<boolean> Close a position fully (deletes a pending). Throws on rejection. closePositionPartial(ticket, volume) Promise<boolean> Close volume lots. Throws on rejection. closeAllPositions() Promise<number> Close every position; returns how many. closeAllBySymbol(symbol) Promise<number> Close all positions on one symbol; returns how many. modifyPositionSL(ticket, sl) Promise<boolean> Set stop-loss (keeps TP). modifyPositionTP(ticket, tp) Promise<boolean> Set take-profit (keeps SL). modifyPositionSLTP(ticket, sl, tp) Promise<boolean> Set both SL and TP.

Two result styles: closePosition / closePositionPartial throw MrpcError on rejection (and return true on success); the modify* methods return false on a non-10009 result instead of throwing. The closeAll* methods skip individual failures and return the count actually closed.

docs.title: 1) Close one position
docs.text: await sugar.closePosition(ticket); // throws if rejected

docs.title: 2) Partial close (half)
docs.text:
const p = await sugar.getPositionByTicket(ticket);
if (p) await sugar.closePositionPartial(ticket, p.volume / 2);

docs.title: 3) Flatten everything
docs.text:
const n = await sugar.closeAllPositions();
console.log(`closed ${n} positions`);

docs.title: 4) Close a basket by symbol
docs.text: await sugar.closeAllBySymbol('EURUSD');

docs.title: 5) Move stop to break-even
docs.text:
const p = await sugar.getPositionByTicket(ticket);
if (p && p.type === 0 && p.priceCurrent > p.priceOpen) { // BUY in profit
  await sugar.modifyPositionSL(ticket, p.priceOpen);
}

docs.title: 6) Set both SL and TP
docs.text:
const ok = await sugar.modifyPositionSLTP(ticket, 1.0800, 1.0950);
console.log(ok ? 'updated' : 'rejected');

docs.title: 🔧 Notes
docs.text:
• Mixed error styles (above) — wrap closePosition* in try/catch; check the boolean for modify*.
  • closeAll* are resilient — a single rejection doesn't abort the batch; the return value is the number closed.
  • Partial close keeps the remainder open with the same ticket.

docs.title: 📚 Related
docs.text:
• Position Information — find the tickets · Simple Trading / SL/TP — open them.
  • Down: MT5Service.closeOrder / modifyOrder.

docs.title: 🎯 Summary
docs.text: Position management sugar covers close (full / partial / all / by symbol) and modify (SL / TP / both). Closes throw on rejection; modifies return a boolean; the batch closers return a count and swallow individual failures.

docs.title: MT5Sugar — Position Information (High-Level API)
docs.text:
Read open positions — all, by ticket, by symbol, counts and floating profit.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — one-liners over MT5Service.getPositions.

Implementation: src/MT5Sugar.ts. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/08_sugar_positions.js.

← MT5Sugar API Overview

docs.title: MT5Sugar — High-Level API Overview
docs.text:
One-line helpers for everyday trading: connect, read balances, quote, buy/sell, manage positions, size risk. The friendliest layer — built on MT5Service, which is built on MT5Account.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — maximum convenience, minimum boilerplate.

docs.title: 🧱 One call builds the whole stack
docs.text:
import { MT5Sugar } from '@metarpc/nodemt5';

const sugar = MT5Sugar.create('mt5.mrpc.pro', 443);
await sugar.quickConnect(login, 'password', 'MetaQuotes-Demo');

const ticket = await sugar.buyMarket('EURUSD', 0.10);
await sugar.modifyPositionSLTP(ticket, 1.0850, 1.1000);
console.log('balance', await sugar.getBalance());
  • MT5Sugar.create(host?, port?, apiKey?, id?) → builds MT5Sugar → MT5Service → MT5Account.
  • sugar.service() → the mid layer · sugar.account() → the low layer. Drop down any time.

docs.title: 🛑 How errors surface
docs.text:
The trading one-liners (buyMarket, closePosition, …) throw MrpcError on a broker rejection (retcode ≠ 10009) — you don't inspect retcodes here, you try/catch:

try {
  const t = await sugar.buyMarket('EURUSD', 0.10);
} catch (e) {
  console.error('rejected:', e.message);
}

Read helpers return plain values; ping() / isConnected() never throw.

docs.title: 📁 Method groups
docs.text: # Group What's inside 1 Connection quickConnect · isConnected · ping 2 Balance & Margin getBalance/Equity/Margin/FreeMargin/MarginLevel/Profit 3 Prices & Quotes getBid/Ask/Spread · getPriceInfo · waitForPrice 4 Simple Trading buy/sellMarket · buy/sellLimit · buy/sellStop 5 Trading with SL/TP buy/sellMarketWithSLTP · buy/sellLimitWithSLTP 6 Position Management closePosition(Partial) · closeAllPositions · modifyPositionSL/TP/SLTP · getOpenPositions 7 Position Information countOpenPositions · hasOpenPosition · getTotalProfit 8 History & Statistics getDeals* · getProfit* 9 Symbol Information getSymbolInfo · getAllSymbols · getMinStopLevel · getSymbolDigits 10 Risk Management calculatePositionSize · getMaxLotSize · canOpenPosition · calculateRequiredMargin · calculateSLTP 11 Trading Helpers buy/sellMarketWithPips 12 Account Information getAccountInfo · getDailyStats

docs.title: 🧮 Pips on MT5
docs.text: Helpers measure "pips" as pipSize = point × (digits is 3 or 5 ? 10 : 1). So on 5-digit EURUSD one pip = 0.0001, on 3-digit JPY pairs one pip = 0.01. SL/TP pip distances everywhere use this convention.

docs.text: • Down: MT5Service — Overview · MT5Account — Master Overview.

docs.title: 11 · Trailing Stop
docs.text:
Open one market BUY, then ratchet its stop-loss up as price advances (never down), and close it at the end — "let winners run, cap the downside".

Run: node examples/demos/main.js 11 · File: examples/demos/orchestrators/11_trailing_stop.js · ⚠ opens one live demo position (tiny cfg.testVolume, self-closing).

← Orchestrators Overview

docs.title: 🎯 What it does
docs.text:
A trailing stop keeps a floating stop-loss a fixed distance behind the market. As price rises the stop follows it up; when price falls the stop stays put. This locks in gains while leaving room for the position to keep running — and guarantees an exit if the move reverses.

This orchestrator is the smallest end-to-end example of managing a position over time: open → watch → adjust → close.

docs.title: 🧠 How it works
docs.text:
buyMarket → loop(cycles):
  read bid → wantSL = bid − trailPips·pip
  if wantSL > bestSL: modifyPositionSL(ticket, wantSL)   // raise only
→ closePosition(ticket)
  1. Select & measure. symbolSelect(sym, true) then getSymbolInfo for digits/point → compute the pip (point × 10 on 3/5-digit symbols, else point).
  2. Open. buyMarket(sym, cfg.testVolume) returns the ticket (throws on a rejection — e.g. market closed — which the demo catches and reports).
  3. Trail. Each cycle: confirm the position is still open (getPositionByTicket), read the bid, compute wantSL = bid − trailPips·pip, and only raise the stop (if wantSL > bestSL). Raising calls modifyPositionSL(ticket, bestSL).
  4. Close. After the cycles, closePosition(ticket).

Ratchet rule. The stop moves up only (wantSL > bestSL). That's what makes it a trailing stop rather than a stop that drifts with every tick.

docs.title: 🎛️ Options
🔑 Key code
docs.text:
let ticket;
try { ticket = await sugar.buyMarket(sym, cfg.testVolume); }
catch (e) { console.log(`rejected (market closed?): ${e.message}`); return; }

let bestSL = 0;
for (let c = 1; c <= cycles; c++) {
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, intervalMs));
  const pos = await sugar.getPositionByTicket(ticket);
  if (!pos) return;                       // closed elsewhere
  const bid = await sugar.getBid(sym);
  const wantSL = bid - trailPips * pip;
  if (wantSL > bestSL) {                   // raise only
    bestSL = wantSL;
    await sugar.modifyPositionSL(ticket, bestSL);
  }
}
await sugar.closePosition(ticket);

docs.title: 🔗 Sugar methods used
docs.text: buyMarket · getBid · getSymbolInfo · getPositionByTicket · modifyPositionSL · closePosition.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & adapting it
docs.text:
• Raise-only is the whole point — drop the wantSL > bestSL guard and it's no longer a trailing stop.
  • Market must be open — buyMarket rejects (10018) out of session; the demo returns gracefully.
  • SELL variant: mirror the geometry — wantSL = ask + trailPips·pip and lower the stop only.
  • Activation threshold: start trailing only once the position is in profit by N pips (compare bid to pos.priceOpen).
  • Real use: replace the fixed cycles loop with a tick stream (streamTicks) and no auto-close.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Grid Trader · Risk Manager · Adaptive Preset
  • MT5Sugar — Position Management — the close/modify helpers it builds on.

docs.title: 13 · Grid Trader
docs.text:
Lay a symmetric grid of pending orders around price — buy-limits below, sell-limits above — list them, then delete the whole grid.

Run: node examples/demos/main.js 13 · File: examples/demos/orchestrators/13_grid_trader.js · ⚠ places small live pending orders on the demo account and deletes them.

← Orchestrators Overview

docs.title: 🎯 What it does
docs.text: A grid strategy brackets the current price with resting orders at regular intervals, so the market triggers entries as it moves either way — a classic approach for range-bound markets. This orchestrator builds the grid, confirms it's live, then tears it down — a complete place → inspect → cancel cycle for pending orders.

docs.title: 🧠 How it works
docs.text:
read bid/ask → for each level i (1..levels):
  buyLimit  @ bid − i·stepPips·pip
  sellLimit @ ask + i·stepPips·pip
→ getOpenedOrders() (count pendings)
→ closePosition(ticket) deletes each pending
  1. Select & measure. symbolSelect, then getSymbolInfo → pip; read bid and ask.
  2. Place the grid. For each level i, a buy-limit i steps below the bid and a sell-limit i steps above the ask. Each buyLimit / sellLimit returns a pending-order ticket (collected in tickets); individual rejections are caught and logged so one bad level doesn't abort the grid.
  3. Inspect. service().getOpenedOrders() returns { positions, orders }; orders are the live pendings — the demo prints the count.
  4. Clean up. closePosition(ticket) on each placed ticket — the same call deletes a pending order as closes a position.

One call, two jobs. closePosition deletes a pending order or closes an open position depending on what the ticket refers to.

docs.title: 🎛️ Options
docs.text:
Option Default Meaning levels 2 Orders per side (so 2 = 2 buy-limits + 2 sell-limits). stepPips 20 Spacing between levels, in pips.

Volume comes from cfg.testVolume.

docs.title: 🔑 Key code
docs.text:
const tickets = [];
for (let i = 1; i <= levels; i++) {
  const below = bid - i * stepPips * pip;
  const above = ask + i * stepPips * pip;
  try { tickets.push(await sugar.buyLimit(sym, volume, below)); } catch (e) { /* log */ }
  try { tickets.push(await sugar.sellLimit(sym, volume, above)); } catch (e) { /* log */ }
}

const { orders } = await sugar.service().getOpenedOrders();
console.log(`pending orders live: ${orders.length}`);

for (const t of tickets) { try { await sugar.closePosition(t); } catch { /* already gone */ } }

docs.title: 🔗 Sugar methods used
docs.text: buyLimit · sellLimit · getBid / getAsk · getSymbolInfo · closePosition · plus service().getOpenedOrders.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & adapting it
docs.text:
• Too close to price rejects. A limit inside the stops/freeze level fails (10016) — keep stepPips comfortably above getMinStopLevel.
  • Resilient placement. Each level is wrapped in try/catch, so a single rejection doesn't abort the grid; if nothing places, the demo returns early.
  • Add SL/TP per level: swap buyLimit → buyLimitWithSLTP.
  • Asymmetric grids: use different levels/stepPips per side, or only one side for a directional bias.
  • Real use: keep the grid alive and refill filled slots instead of deleting everything.

docs.text:

  • MT5Sugar — Simple Trading — the order helpers.

docs.title: 14 · Risk Manager
docs.text:
Monitor account health each cycle — equity, margin level, floating P/L, open positions — and flatten everything if drawdown or margin breaches a limit. A protective kill-switch.

Run: node examples/demos/main.js 14 · File: examples/demos/orchestrators/14_risk_manager.js · ⛔ read-only until a limit breaks, then it closes all positions.

← Orchestrators Overview

docs.title: 🎯 What it does
docs.text: This orchestrator watches the account rather than the chart. Each cycle it reads health metrics and checks them against two limits; if either breaks, it closes every open position and stops. It's the pattern you'd run alongside a trading strategy as a safety net — the one orchestrator that places no orders of its own (except the protective close).

docs.title: 🧠 How it works
docs.text:
startBalance = getBalance()
loop(cycles):
  read equity, marginLevel, floating P/L, open count
  ddPct = (startBalance − equity) / startBalance · 100
  if ddPct > maxDrawdownPct  OR  (open>0 and marginLevel < minMarginLevel):
      closeAllPositions()   ← kill-switch, then stop
  1. Baseline. getBalance() once, up front, as the drawdown reference.
  2. Read health (read-only). Each cycle: getAccountInfo() (equity, marginLevel), getTotalProfit() (summed floating P/L), countOpenPositions().
  3. Evaluate. Compute drawdown ddPct from startBalance vs equity. A breach is ddPct > maxDrawdownPct or (positions open and 0 < marginLevel < minMarginLevel).
  4. Kill-switch. On a breach, closeAllPositions() (returns how many it closed) and return. Otherwise wait intervalMs and loop.

Margin guard is conditional. The margin check only fires when positions are open and marginLevel > 0 — a flat account (margin level 0) never trips it.

docs.title: 🎛️ Options
docs.text: Option Default Meaning maxDrawdownPct 5 Max equity drawdown from the start balance, %. minMarginLevel 150 Minimum margin level, % (below → breach). cycles 5 How many times to check. intervalMs 800 Delay between checks, ms.

docs.title: 🔑 Key code
docs.text:
const startBalance = await sugar.getBalance();

for (let c = 1; c <= cycles; c++) {
  const a = await sugar.getAccountInfo();
  const floating = await sugar.getTotalProfit();
  const open = await sugar.countOpenPositions();
  const ddPct = startBalance > 0 ? ((startBalance - a.equity) / startBalance) * 100 : 0;

  const breach = ddPct > maxDrawdownPct || (open > 0 && a.marginLevel > 0 && a.marginLevel < minMarginLevel);
  if (breach) {
    const closed = await sugar.closeAllPositions();   // kill-switch
    console.log(`⚠ LIMIT BREACHED — closed ${closed}`);
    return;
  }
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, intervalMs));
}

docs.title: 🔗 Sugar methods used
docs.text: getBalance · getAccountInfo · getTotalProfit · countOpenPositions · closeAllPositions.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & adapting it
docs.text:
• Safe to run anytime. With no open positions it just reports and never trips — the kill-switch only closes what exists.
  • Pair it with a strategy. Run this loop next to Trailing Stop / Grid Trader as an independent guard.
  • Add a daily-loss limit: combine with getDailyStats (totalProfit <= −limit).
  • Partial de-risking: instead of flattening everything, close only the worst positions (sort getOpenPositions by profit).
  • Real use: make it a long-lived loop (or timer) rather than a fixed cycle count.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Trailing Stop · Grid Trader · Adaptive Preset
  • MT5Sugar — Risk Management — pre-trade sizing & checks.

docs.title: 16 · Adaptive Preset
docs.text:
A preset coordinates orchestrators behind one decision: read recent bars, classify the market, and dispatch to the orchestrator that fits — trend, range or volatility.

Run: node examples/demos/main.js 16 · File: examples/demos/presets/16_adaptive_preset.js · ↪ delegates to whichever orchestrator it picks (so it may place demo orders via that one).

← Orchestrators Overview

docs.title: 🎯 What it is
docs.text:
Where an orchestrator runs one strategy, a preset chooses which strategy to run. This one reads the recent price action, decides whether the market is trending, ranging or volatile, and hands off to the matching orchestrator:

Market mode → Orchestrator Rationale TRENDING Trailing Stop ride the move RANGING Grid Trader fade the range VOLATILE Risk Manager stay defensive

docs.title: 🧠 How it works
docs.text:
priceHistory(sym, 'H1', { maxBars: 20 })
  avgRange = mean(high − low)
  trend    = |lastClose − firstClose| / avgRange      // net move, in ranges
  spike    = max(high − low) / avgRange               // biggest bar vs average
→ mode = spike > 2.5 ? VOLATILE : trend > 2.0 ? TRENDING : RANGING
→ run the chosen orchestrator
  1. Gather bars. service().priceHistory(sym, 'H1', { maxBars: 20 }). Fewer than 5 bars → default to RANGING (grid).
  2. Derive two ratios. trend = net directional move measured in average ranges; spike = the largest single bar relative to the average — a volatility proxy.
  3. Classify. spike > 2.5 → VOLATILE; else trend > 2.0 → TRENDING; else RANGING.
  4. Dispatch. Call the matching orchestrator with the same (sugar, cfg) — each then runs its own API calls.

Thresholds are illustrative. 2.5 (spike) and 2.0 (trend) are tuned for a teaching demo on H1 bars — adjust them for your timeframe and instrument.

docs.title: 🔑 Key code
docs.text:
const bars = await sugar.service().priceHistory(sym, 'H1', { maxBars: 20 });
if (bars.length < 5) return gridTrader(sugar, cfg);        // default: RANGING

let sumRange = 0, maxRange = 0;
for (const b of bars) { const r = b.high - b.low; sumRange += r; maxRange = Math.max(maxRange, r); }
const avgRange = sumRange / bars.length;
const move  = Math.abs(bars[bars.length - 1].close - bars[0].close);
const trend = avgRange > 0 ? move / avgRange : 0;
const spike = avgRange > 0 ? maxRange / avgRange : 1;

const mode = spike > 2.5 ? 'VOLATILE' : trend > 2.0 ? 'TRENDING' : 'RANGING';
if (mode === 'VOLATILE') return riskManager(sugar, cfg);
if (mode === 'TRENDING') return trailingStop(sugar, cfg);
return gridTrader(sugar, cfg);

Orchestrators are plain modules, so the preset just requires and calls them:

const trailingStop = require('../orchestrators/11_trailing_stop');
const gridTrader   = require('../orchestrators/13_grid_trader');
const riskManager  = require('../orchestrators/14_risk_manager');

docs.title: 🔗 Built on
docs.text: service().priceHistory + the three orchestrators (11 · 13 · 14). It adds no trading calls of its own — all orders come from the orchestrator it dispatches to.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & adapting it
docs.text:
• Composition, not inheritance. A preset is just a function that calls other functions — the cleanest way to coordinate strategies.
  • Deterministic fallback. Too little history → RANGING, so the preset always does something sensible.
  • Better classifiers: swap the two ratios for ATR, ADX, or a regime model — the dispatch structure stays the same.
  • More modes: add e.g. QUIET → do nothing, or BREAKOUT → a stop-grid.
  • Schedule it: run the preset on a timer so the chosen mode re-evaluates as conditions change.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Orchestrators Overview — the shared shape & safety notes.
  • Trailing Stop · Grid Trader · Risk Manager — the strategies it dispatches to.

docs.title: Orchestrators — Overview
docs.text:
Small, self-contained strategy loops built entirely on MT5Sugar. Each is a plain async function demo(sugar, cfg, opts) you can read, run on the demo account, and adapt.

These are teaching examples of coordinating the SDK over time — not production trading systems. They show how the one-liners compose into a working loop.

docs.title: 🧩 Orchestrator vs preset
docs.text:
• An orchestrator runs one strategy end-to-end (open → manage → close, or monitor → act).
  • A preset picks which orchestrator to run from the current market conditions, then delegates to it.

So the three orchestrators are the strategies; the preset is the coordinator on top.

docs.title: 📁 What's here
docs.text:
# File Idea Writes trades? 11 Trailing Stop Open a BUY, ratchet its SL up as price advances, close. ✅ one position 13 Grid Trader Lay a symmetric grid of pending limits, list, delete. ✅ pending orders 14 Risk Manager Monitor equity / margin / drawdown; kill-switch on breach. ⛔ read-only unless a limit breaks 16 Adaptive Preset Classify the market, dispatch to the matching orchestrator. ↪ delegates

The numbering follows the demo files (examples/demos/orchestrators/, .../presets/). Slots 12 & 15 from the Go reference set are intentionally not ported.

docs.title: How the preset composes them
docs.text:
┌──────────────── 16 Adaptive Preset ───────────────┐
  priceHistory → │ TRENDING → 11 Trailing   RANGING → 13 Grid        │
                 │                 VOLATILE → 14 Risk Manager        │
                 └───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 🧱 The shape they share
docs.text:
module.exports = async function demo(sugar, cfg, opts = {}) {
  // sugar : a connected MT5Sugar
  // cfg   : { testSymbol, testVolume, ... }  (from examples/demos/config)
  // opts  : per-run tuning (cycles, pips, thresholds…)
};
  • sugar — a connected MT5Sugar; reach down with sugar.service() / sugar.account().
  • cfg — testSymbol and testVolume drive what and how much; shared across demos.
  • opts — each orchestrator documents its own knobs (trail distance, grid levels, risk limits…).

Run any of them from the demo menu:

node examples/demos/main.js 11      # trailing stop
node examples/demos/main.js 13      # grid trader
node examples/demos/main.js 14      # risk manager
node examples/demos/main.js 16      # adaptive preset

docs.title: 🧠 Shared building blocks
docs.text:
All four lean on the same handful of sugar calls:

Concern Sugar methods Price & spec getBid / getAsk · getSymbolInfo · service().priceHistory Enter buyMarket / buyLimit / sellLimit Manage modifyPositionSL · closePosition / closeAllPositions Watch getAccountInfo · getTotalProfit / countOpenPositions / getPositionByTicket

The pip convention is shared too: pip = point × (digits is 3 or 5 ? 10 : 1).

docs.title: ⚠️ Safety
docs.text: 11, 13 and 16 place live orders on the configured demo account (tiny cfg.testVolume, self-closing). 14 is read-only until a risk limit is breached, at which point it closes everything. Never point these at a real account while learning.
